title.zh: 卷八十六 南蠻西南夷列傳
title.en: Volume 86: Treatise on the Nanman, Southwestern Barbarians
title.raw: 卷八十六 南蠻西南夷列傳 Volume 86: Treatise on the Nanman, Southwestern Barbarians

sentences.zh: 昔高辛氏有犬戎之寇，帝患其侵暴，而征伐不克。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Gaoxin clan had Quanrong marauders; the emperor worried at their invasion and violence, yet campaigns could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient Emperor Ku faced the Quanrong raiders: punitive expeditions failed to stop their violence.

sentences.zh: 乃訪募天下，有能得犬戎之將吳將軍頭者，購黄金千镒，邑萬家，又妻以少女。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sought and recruited under Heaven: whoever could obtain the head of Quanrong general Wu Jiangjun—reward a thousand yi of gold, a settlement of ten thousand households, and moreover give him a young girl as wife.
translations.idiomatic: He offered a thousand yi of gold, a fief of ten thousand households, and an imperial princess to whoever brought in General Wu's head.

sentences.zh: 時帝有畜狗，其毛五采，名曰槃瓠。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had a kept dog; its fur was five-colored; its name was Panhu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor owned a five-colored hound named Panhu.

sentences.zh: 下令之后，槃瓠遂衔人頭造阙下，群臣怪而診之，乃吳將軍首也。

translations.literal: After the order issued, Panhu then bore a human head in its mouth and arrived below the palace gate; the various ministers wondered and examined it—it was Wu Jiangjun's head.
translations.idiomatic: Panhu soon laid General Wu's severed head at the palace gate for all to verify.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，而計槃瓠不可妻之以女，又無封爵之道，議欲有報而未知所宜。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, but reckoned that Panhu could not be given a daughter as wife, and there was no way to enfeoff rank; they deliberated wishing to have recompense but did not know what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The court rejoiced yet hesitated—how marry a dog or grant it nobility?—while owing a reward.

sentences.zh: 女聞之，以為帝皇下令，不可違信，因請行。

translations.literal: The girl heard it; she considered that the emperor had issued an order and trust could not be violated; thereupon she requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: The princess held the proclamation binding and volunteered to go.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，乃以女配槃瓠。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice; thereupon he matched the girl to Panhu.
translations.idiomatic: Yielding to necessity, he gave her to Panhu.

sentences.zh: 槃瓠得女，負而走入南山，止石室中。

translations.literal: Panhu obtained the girl; carrying her on his back he entered the southern mountains and stopped in a stone chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Panhu shouldered his bride into the southern hills and sheltered in a stone cave.

sentences.zh: 所處險絕，人迹不至。

translations.literal: The place they dwelt was perilous and cut off; human tracks did not reach there.
translations.idiomatic: The refuge lay in trackless, precipitous wilds.

sentences.zh: 于是女解去衣裳，為僕鉴之結，着獨力之衣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the girl removed upper and lower garments, made a servant-mirror knot, and wore single-strength clothing.
translations.idiomatic: She shed court dress for rustic wraps suited to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 帝悲思之，遣使尋求，輒遇風雨震晦，使者不得進。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved and thought of her; he dispatched envoys to seek; they always met wind and rain, thunder and dark; envoys could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Search parties turned back before storms and darkness blocked every path.

sentences.zh: 经三年，生子一十二人，六男六女。

translations.literal: After three years passed, they bore children twelve persons—six males and six females.
translations.idiomatic: Three years brought twelve children, evenly split between sons and daughters.

sentences.zh: 槃瓠死后，因自相夫妻。

translations.literal: After Panhu died, they thereupon paired themselves as husbands and wives.
translations.idiomatic: After Panhu died, the siblings intermarried among themselves.

sentences.zh: 織績木皮，染以草實，好五色衣服。

translations.literal: They wove and spun tree bark, dyed with grass seeds; they loved five-colored clothing.
translations.idiomatic: They wove bark cloth dyed from berries into bright patterned dress.

sentences.zh: 制裁皆有尾形。

translations.literal: Clothing cutting all had tail shapes.
translations.idiomatic: Their garments were cut with trailing ends like tails.

sentences.zh: 其母后歸，以状白帝，于是使迎致諸子。

translations.literal: Their mother later returned; she reported the situation to the emperor; thereupon he sent to welcome and bring the various children.
translations.idiomatic: When the mother finally reached court and told her tale, the emperor summoned the children down from the hills.

sentences.zh: 衣裳班兰，語言侏離，好入山壑，不乐平曠。

translations.literal: Robes and skirts were mottled and bright; speech was zhu-li; they loved to enter mountain ravines; they did not delight in flat openness.
translations.idiomatic: They wore parti-colored clothes, spoke a guttural tongue, and preferred ravines to open plains.

sentences.zh: 帝顺其意，賜以名山廣澤。

translations.literal: The emperor followed their intent and bestowed on them famous mountains and broad marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring their wishes, he granted them titled hills and wide wetlands.

sentences.zh: 其后滋蔓，号曰蠻夷。

translations.literal: Afterward they spread and branched; they were titled Man and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Their descendants multiplied into the peoples called Man and Yi.

sentences.zh: 外痴内黠，安土重旧。

translations.literal: Outwardly foolish, inwardly crafty; they secure soil and esteem the old.
translations.idiomatic: They seem simple but are shrewd, deeply attached to homeland and ancient ways.

sentences.zh: 以先父有功，母帝之女，田作贾贩，無关梁符传、租税之赋。

translations.literal: Because their former father had merit and their mother was the emperor's daughter, they farmed and traded—without barrier-pass tokens or rent-tax levies.
translations.idiomatic: As heirs of a meritorious forebear and an imperial daughter, they farmed and peddled free of tolls and grain taxes.

sentences.zh: 有邑君长，皆賜印绶，冠用獭皮。

translations.literal: Where there were settlement lords and chiefs, all were bestowed seal-cords; caps used otter fur.
translations.idiomatic: Local headmen received Han seals and wore otter-skin caps.

sentences.zh: 名渠帅曰精夫，相呼為姎徒。

translations.literal: They named channel leaders jingfu; they called one another yangtu.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs were styled jingfu; people hailed each other as yangtu.

sentences.zh: 今长沙武陵蠻是也。

translations.literal: Today's Changsha and Wuling Man are these.
translations.idiomatic: These are the ancestors of today's Changsha and Wuling Man.

sentences.zh: 其在唐、虞，与之要質，故曰要服。

translations.literal: In the time of Tang and Yu, with them there was hostage covenant; therefore it is called yaofu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yao and Shun they exchanged hostages—hence the "covenant quarter" of the nine domains.

sentences.zh: 夏、商之時，漸為边患。

translations.literal: In the time of Xia and Shang, they gradually became a border peril.
translations.idiomatic: By Xia and Shang they had turned into a frontier threat.

sentences.zh: 逮于周世，党众弥盛。

translations.literal: By the Zhou age, factions and crowds grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou their numbers swelled.

sentences.zh: 宣王中興，乃命方叔南伐蠻方，詩人所謂“蠻荆来威”者也。

translations.literal: King Xuan's restoration—thereupon he ordered Fang Shu to campaign south against Manfang; it is what the poets call "Man-Jing came in awe."
translations.idiomatic: Restored King Xuan sent Fang Shu south—the "Man of Jing submit in awe" line in the Odes.

sentences.zh: 又曰：“蠢尔蠻荆，大邦為仇。

translations.literal: It also says: "You foolish Man-Jing, you make the great state your foe."
translations.idiomatic: Another ode taunts: "Insolent Man of Jing—you dare rival the great realm."

sentences.zh: ”明其党众繁多，是以抗敌諸夏也。

translations.literal: "It clarifies that their party crowd was many and numerous; therefore they resisted the various Xia."
translations.idiomatic: The verse shows their hosts were vast enough to defy the central states."

sentences.zh: 平王东迁，蠻遂侵暴上國。

translations.literal: When King Ping moved east, the Man thereupon invaded and oppressed the upper states.
translations.idiomatic: After King Ping relocated east, the Man raided the heartland.

sentences.zh: 晉文侯輔政，乃率蔡共侯擊破之。

translations.literal: When Marquis Wen of Jin assisted government, he then led Marquis Gong of Cai to attack and break them.
translations.idiomatic: Regent Marquis Wen of Jin and Cai's ruler drove them back.

sentences.zh: 至楚武王時，蠻与罗子共败楚師，殺其將屈瑕。

translations.literal: By the time of King Wu of Chu, the Man together with the ruler of Luo defeated Chu forces and killed their general Qu Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Wu of Chu the Man and Luo allies shattered Chu and slew Qu Xia.

sentences.zh: 庄王初立，民饥兵弱，復為所寇。

translations.literal: When King Zhuang first ascended, the people starved and troops were weak; again they were raided by them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in King Zhuang's reign famine and weak arms let the Man strike again.

sentences.zh: 楚師既振。

translations.literal: After Chu forces had revived.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chu recovered its strength

sentences.zh: 然后乃服，自是遂屬于楚。

translations.literal: only then did they submit; from this they thereupon belonged to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: the Man yielded and thereafter answered to Chu.

sentences.zh: 鄢陵之役，蠻与恭王合兵擊晉。

translations.literal: At the battle of Yanling, the Man together with King Gong combined troops to strike Jin.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanling they fought beside King Gong of Chu against Jin.

sentences.zh: 及吳起相悼王，南并蠻越，遂有洞庭、苍梧。

translations.literal: When Wu Qi was minister to King Dao, he annexed southward Man and Yue; thereupon he held Dongting and Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qi's southern campaigns for King Dao absorbed Man and Yue lands to Dongting and Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 秦昭王使白起伐楚，略取蠻夷，始置黔中郡。

translations.literal: King Zhaoxiang of Qin sent Bai Qi to campaign against Chu, seized and took Man and Yi, and first established Qianzhong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Qi's offensive carved out the Man lands as Qianzhong commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢興，改為武陵。

translations.literal: When Han rose, it was changed to Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: The Han renamed the region Wuling.

sentences.zh: 岁令大人輸布一匹，小口二丈，是謂賨布。

translations.literal: Each year it ordered great men to remit one bolt of cloth, minors two zhang; this is called cong cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Adults paid one bolt of cloth yearly, children two zhang—the "tribute cloth."

sentences.zh: 雖時為寇盗，而不足為郡國患。

translations.literal: Although at times they were raiding bandits, they were insufficient to be a peril to commanderies and states.
translations.idiomatic: Occasional banditry never seriously threatened the commanderies.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，武陵蠻夷特盛。

translations.literal: At Guangwu's restoration, Wuling Man and Yi were especially strong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu's revival found Wuling's tribes unusually powerful.

sentences.zh: 建武二十三年，精夫相单程等据其險隘，大寇郡縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Jianwu, jingfu Xiang Dancheng and others occupied their perilous passes and greatly raided commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 47: chiefs such as Xiang Dancheng held the defiles and overran the lowlands.

sentences.zh: 遣武威將軍劉尚发南郡、长沙、武陵兵萬余人，乘船溯沅水，入武谿擊之。

translations.literal: He dispatched General Weiwu Liu Shang to mobilize more than ten thousand troops of Nan commandery, Changsha, and Wuling; ride boats and ascend the Yuan River; enter Wuxi and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: General Liu Shang took ten thousand men up the Yuan into Wuxi gorge.

sentences.zh: 尚轻敌入險，山深水疾，舟船不得上。

translations.literal: Shang belittled the enemy and entered hazards; mountains were high, water swift; boats and ships could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shang underestimated the terrain: rapids and cliffs stopped his fleet.

sentences.zh: 蠻氏知尚粮少入遠，又不晓道径，遂屯聚守險。

translations.literal: The Man clans knew Shang had little grain and had penetrated far; moreover they did not know paths; thereupon they gathered and guarded hazards.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes knew he was short of supplies and lost in the maze of trails; they massed on the heights.

sentences.zh: 尚食尽引还，蠻缘路徼戰，尚軍大败，悉為所没。

translations.literal: When Shang's food was exhausted he led a withdrawal; the Man along the road intercepted battle; Shang's army was greatly defeated; all were engulfed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Starving, Shang retreated into ambushes and lost his entire command.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，相单程等下攻临沅，遣谒者李嵩、中山太守馬成擊之，不能克。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Xiang Dancheng and others descended and attacked Linyuan; he dispatched Herald Li Song and Zhongshan governor Ma Cheng to strike them; they could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 48: the Man struck Linyuan; Li Song and Ma Cheng failed to dislodge them.

sentences.zh: 明年春，遣伏波將軍馬援、中郎將劉匡、馬武、孫永等，將兵至临沅，擊破之。

translations.literal: The next spring, he dispatched General Fubo Ma Yuan, generals of the Gentlemen of the Household Liu Kuang, Ma Wu, Sun Yong, and others; they led troops to Linyuan and attacked and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring Ma Yuan and his lieutenants crushed the rebels at Linyuan.

sentences.zh: 单程等饥困乞降，会援病卒，谒者宗均听悉受降。

translations.literal: Dancheng and others, hungry and distressed, begged to surrender; it happened that Yuan died of illness; Herald Zong Jun listened and accepted all surrenders.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sued for peace when supplies failed; Ma Yuan died before the finish, but Herald Zong Jun accepted wholesale capitulation.

sentences.zh: 為置吏司，群蠻遂平。

translations.literal: For them he set up clerks and offices; the various Man thereupon were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Han installed magistrates and the tribes quieted.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元四年冬，溇中、澧中蠻潭戎等反，燔烧邮亭，殺略吏民，郡兵擊破降之。

translations.literal: In winter of Emperor He's Yongyuan fourth year, Louzhong and Lizhong Man Tan Rong and others rebelled; they burned postal stations, killed and seized officials and people; commandery troops attacked, broke, and made them surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyuan 92 winter: Tan Rong's bands torched relay stations until county troops forced their surrender.

sentences.zh: 安帝元初二年，澧中蠻以郡縣徭税失平，怀怨恨，遂結充中諸种二千余人，攻城殺长吏。

translations.literal: In Emperor An's Yuanchu second year, Lizhong Man because commandery county corvée tax was unfair harbored resentment; thereupon they allied Chongzhong various kinds more than two thousand persons; attacked cities and killed senior officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchu 115: Lizhong tribes, resenting uneven taxes, joined two thousand Chongzhong warriors to storm towns and murder prefects.

sentences.zh: 州郡募五里蠻六亭兵追擊破之，皆散降。

translations.literal: Province and commandery recruited Wuli Man and Liuting troops to pursue attack and break them; all scattered and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial levies from allied Man villages ran them down until they dissolved and yielded.

sentences.zh: 賜五里、六亭渠帅金帛各有差。

translations.literal: They bestowed on Wuli and Liuting channel leaders gold and silk each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal chiefs of Wuli and Liuting received graded gifts of bullion and silk.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，溇中、澧中蠻四千人并為盗贼。

translations.literal: The next autumn, Louzhong and Lizhong Man four thousand persons together became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Next fall four thousand Louzhong and Lizhong warriors turned outlaw.

sentences.zh: 又零陵蠻羊孫、陳汤等千余人，著赤帻，称將軍，烧官寺，抄掠百姓。

translations.literal: Also Lingling Man Yang Sun, Chen Tang, and others more than a thousand persons wore red ze; titled themselves generals; burned official temples; plundered common people.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand Lingling rebels under Yang Sun and Chen Tang donned red turbans, styled themselves generals, and pillaged shrines and villages.

sentences.zh: 州郡募善蠻討平之。

translations.literal: Province and commandery recruited friendly Man and campaigned to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities hired loyal Man auxiliaries to restore order.

sentences.zh: 顺帝永和元年，武陵太守上書，以蠻夷率服，可比漢人，增其租赋。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shun's Yonghe first year, the Wuling governor submitted a memorial: because Man and Yi generally submit, they may be compared to Han people—increase their rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe 136: the Wuling governor argued the tribes were docile enough to tax like Han subjects.

sentences.zh: 議者皆以為可。

translations.literal: Discussants all thought it acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Most advisers agreed.

sentences.zh: 尚書令虞诩獨奏曰：“自古圣王，不臣异俗，非德不能及，威不能加，知其兽心贪婪，难率以礼。

translations.literal: Minister Director Yu Xu alone submitted: "From antiquity sage kings do not treat alien customs as subjects—not virtue cannot reach them, might cannot impose; knowing their beast hearts are greedy, hard to lead with ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Clerk Yu Xu dissented: sage kings never fully Sinicized barbarians—virtue and fear alike fail against greedy natures untamed by ritual."

sentences.zh: 是故羁縻而绶抚之，附則受而不逆，叛則弃而不追。

translations.literal: Therefore halter-rein them and soothe them with seal-cords; if they attach then accept and do not oppose; if they rebel then abandon and do not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Hence loose rein: welcome allies without forcing uniformity, drop rebels without chasing forever."

sentences.zh: 先帝旧典，贡税多少，所由来久矣。

translations.literal: Former emperors' old statutes—how much tribute tax—what comes from this has been long.
translations.idiomatic: The founding precedents on tribute levels have stood for generations."

sentences.zh: 今猥增之，必有怨叛。

translations.literal: Now rashly increasing them—there must be resentment and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden hikes will breed resentment and revolt."

sentences.zh: 計其所得，不偿所费，必有后悔。

translations.literal: Reckon what is obtained—it does not repay what is expended—there must be later regret.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue will not cover the cost of pacification—you will rue it."

sentences.zh: ”帝不从。

translations.literal: "The emperor did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored him.

sentences.zh: 其冬、澧中、溇中蠻果争贡布非旧约，遂殺乡吏，舉种反叛。

translations.literal: That winter Lizhong and Louzhong Man indeed disputed tribute cloth not matching old covenant; thereupon they killed village clerks; whole kinds rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Lizhong and Louzhong disputed the new cloth levy, slew headmen, and rose en masse.

sentences.zh: 明年春，蠻二萬人围充城，八千人寇夷道。

translations.literal: The next spring, twenty thousand Man besieged Chong city; eight thousand raided Yidao.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring twenty thousand laid siege to Chong while eight thousand struck Yidao.

sentences.zh: 遣武陵太守李進討破之，斬首數百級，余皆降服。

translations.literal: He dispatched Wuling governor Li Jin to campaign and break them; several hundred heads beheaded; the rest all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Li Jin routed them, took several hundred heads, and accepted the rest.

sentences.zh: 進乃简选良吏，得其情和。

translations.literal: Jin thereupon selected good clerks; obtained their feelings harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jin then posted honest officials and restored harmony.

sentences.zh: 在郡九年，梁太后临朝，下詔增進秩二千石，賜钱二十萬。

translations.literal: He was in the commandery nine years; Empress Dowager Liang faced court; issued edict increasing Jin's rank two thousand shi; bestowed two hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years Empress Dowager Liang promoted him to two-thousand-shi rank with two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 桓帝元嘉元年秋，武陵蠻詹山等四千余人反叛，拘执縣令，屯結深山。

translations.literal: In autumn of Emperor Huan's Yuanjia first year, Wuling Man Zhan Shan and others more than four thousand rebelled; seized and held the county magistrate; gathered and massed in deep mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjia 151 autumn: Zhan Shan led four thousand Wuling Man who seized their magistrate and entrenched in the hills.

sentences.zh: 至永興元年，太守应奉以恩信招誘，皆悉降散。

translations.literal: By Yongxing first year, governor Ying Feng with grace and trust summoned and enticed; all surrendered and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: By Yongxing 153 Governor Ying Feng talked them down with promises.

sentences.zh: 永寿三年十一月，长沙蠻反叛，屯益阳。

translations.literal: In eleventh month of Yongshou third year, Changsha Man rebelled and massed at Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshou 157: Changsha tribes rebelled and camped at Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 至延熹三年秋，遂抄掠郡界，众至萬余人，殺伤长吏。

translations.literal: By Yanxi third year autumn, they thereupon raided the commandery border; crowds reached more than ten thousand persons; killed and wounded senior officials.
translations.idiomatic: By Yanxi 160 autumn over ten thousand raided the commandery and wounded prefects.

sentences.zh: 又零陵蠻入长沙。

translations.literal: Also Lingling Man entered Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Lingling tribes joined the thrust into Changsha.

sentences.zh: 冬，武陵蠻六千余人寇江陵，荆州刺史劉度、谒者馬睦、南郡太守李肃皆奔走。

translations.literal: In winter more than six thousand Wuling Man raided Jiangling; Jingzhou inspector Liu Du, Herald Ma Mu, Nan commandery governor Li Su all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Winter: six thousand Wuling warriors took Jiangling while Liu Du, Ma Mu, and Li Su fled.

sentences.zh: 肃主簿胡爽扣馬首谏曰：“蠻夷见郡無儆备，故敢乘間而進。

translations.literal: Li Su's chief clerk Hu Shuang seized the horse's head and remonstrated: "Man and Yi see the commandery without alert preparation; therefore dare exploit intervals and advance.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shuang seized the bridle: "The tribes strike because they see no defenses—"

sentences.zh: 明府為國大臣，連城千里，舉旄鸣鼓，应声十萬，奈何委符守之重，而為逋逃之人乎！

translations.literal: Bright prefect is the state's great minister; linked cities a thousand li; raise banner and beat drum—a hundred thousand respond to sound—how abandon seal-guarding weight and become a fleeing fugitive person!
translations.idiomatic: you command a thousand li—ten thousand arms answer your drum—how can you cast aside your seal and run like a coward!"

sentences.zh: ”肃拔刃向爽曰：“掾促去！

translations.literal: "Su drew blade toward Shuang and said: "Clerk, hasten away!
translations.idiomatic: Li Su drew steel: "Out of my way, clerk!"

sentences.zh: 太守今急，何暇此計。

translations.literal: The governor now is pressed—what leisure for this plan.
translations.idiomatic: I'm fleeing for my life—no time for lectures."

sentences.zh: ”爽抱馬固谏，肃遂殺爽而走。

translations.literal: "Shuang embraced the horse and firmly remonstrated; Su thereupon killed Shuang and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shuang clung to the reins until Li Su cut him down and rode off.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，征肃弃市，度、睦减死一等，復爽门闾，拜家一人為郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he summoned Su for execution in the market; Du and Mu had death reduced one grade; restored Shuang's gate and lane; appointed one family member gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The court executed Li Su in the marketplace, reduced sentences on Liu Du and Ma Mu, honored Hu Shuang's kin, and ennobled a son.

sentences.zh: 于是以右校令度尚為荆州刺史，討长沙贼，平之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made Right Superintendent Du Shang Jingzhou inspector; campaigned against Changsha bandits; pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shang became inspector and crushed the Changsha rebels.

sentences.zh: 又遣车骑將軍冯绲討武陵蠻，并皆降散。

translations.literal: He also dispatched chariot-and-cavalry general Feng Juan to campaign against Wuling Man; together all surrendered and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: General Feng Juan dispersed the Wuling rising.

sentences.zh: 軍还，贼復寇桂阳，太守瘳析奔走。

translations.literal: When the army returned, bandits again raided Guiyang; governor Liao Xi fled.
translations.idiomatic: On withdrawal the rebels hit Guiyang and Governor Liao Xi bolted.

sentences.zh: 武陵蠻亦更攻其郡，太守陳奉率吏人擊破之，斬首三千余級，降者二千余人。

translations.literal: Wuling Man also again attacked their commandery; governor Chen Feng led clerks and people to attack and break them; more than three thousand heads beheaded; more than two thousand surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wuling tribes struck again until Chen Feng killed three thousand and accepted two thousand surrenders.

sentences.zh: 至靈帝中平三年，武陵蠻復叛，寇郡界，州郡擊破之。

translations.literal: By Emperor Ling's Zhongping third year, Wuling Man again rebelled; raided commandery border; province and commandery attacked and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongping 186: another Wuling revolt ended in defeat.

sentences.zh: 《礼记》称“南方曰蠻，雕题交阯”。

translations.literal: The "Record of Rites" states "the south is called Man—carved foreheads, intersecting toes."
translations.idiomatic: The "Book of Rites" calls the south "Man"—tattooed brows and the "Interleaved Toes" land.

sentences.zh: 其俗男女同川而浴，故曰交阯。

translations.literal: Their custom: men and women bathe together in the same stream; therefore it is called Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women shared riverside baths—hence the name Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 其西有噉人國，生首子輒解而食之，謂之宜弟。

translations.literal: West of them there is a man-eating state; when the firstborn son is born they invariably butcher and eat him; they call it "fitting younger brother."
translations.idiomatic: Westward lies a cannibal realm that sacrifices firstborns for luck—"feeding the younger brother."

sentences.zh: 味旨，則以遗其君，君喜而赏其父。

translations.literal: If the flavor is delicious, then they present it to their lord; the lord is pleased and rewards the father.
translations.idiomatic: Choice cuts go to the chief, who rewards the father.

sentences.zh: 取妻美，則让其兄。

translations.literal: If taking a wife beautiful, then they yield to elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: A beautiful bride they cede to an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 今烏滸人是也。

translations.literal: Today's Wuhu people are these.
translations.idiomatic: These are the modern Wuhu tribes.

sentences.zh: 交阯之南有越裳國。

translations.literal: South of Jiaozhi there is Yueshang state.
translations.idiomatic: South of Jiaozhi lies Yueshang.

sentences.zh: 周公居摄六年，制礼作乐，天下和平，越裳以三象重譯而献白雉，曰：“道路悠遠，山川阻深，音使不通，故重譯而朝。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Zhou acted as regent six years, instituted ritual and made music; under Heaven was peaceful; Yueshang through three relays of interpreters presented a white pheasant, saying: "Roads and paths are long and far; mountains and streams obstruct and are deep; sounds and envoys do not penetrate; therefore repeated interpreters and audience.
translations.idiomatic: Regent Zhou's peace drew Yueshang envoys through triple interpreters with a white pheasant: "Distance and rugged terrain force relayed translation."

sentences.zh: ”成王以歸周公。

translations.literal: "King Cheng thereby gave it to the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng forwarded the gift to the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 公曰：“德不加焉，則君子不飨其質；

translations.literal: The Duke said: "If virtue does not extend there, then the gentleman does not feast on their tribute;
translations.idiomatic: The Duke replied: "Without virtue abroad we do not accept distant tribute—"

sentences.zh: 政不施焉，則君子不臣其人。

translations.literal: if governance is not applied there, then the gentleman does not treat those people as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: without civilizing rule we do not claim them as subjects."

sentences.zh: 吾何以获此賜也！

translations.literal: How did I obtain this gift!
translations.idiomatic: How have I earned such an honor!

sentences.zh: ”其使請曰：“吾受命吾國之黄耉曰：‘久矣，天之無烈風雷雨，意者中國有圣人乎？

translations.literal: "Their envoy requested and said: "I received charge from my state's hoary elders: 'Long already—Heaven has had no fierce wind, thunder, or rain—perhaps the Central States have a sage?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy explained: his gray-haired elders had sent word—"No storms rage over us; perhaps a sage rules China?"

sentences.zh: 有則盍往朝之。

translations.literal: If there is one, why not go and court him.
translations.idiomatic: If so, we should present ourselves at his court."

sentences.zh: ’”周公乃歸之于王，称先王之神致，以荐于宗庙。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou then presented it to the king, invoking the spiritual blessing of the former kings, and offered it in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou passed the gift to King Cheng and lodged it in the Zhou ancestral shrine as a token from the departed kings."

sentences.zh: 周德既衰，于是稍絕。

translations.literal: Zhou virtue having declined, from this it gradually broke off.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou's moral prestige faded, Yueshang contact lapsed.

sentences.zh: 及楚子称霸，朝贡百越。

translations.literal: When the Chu lord held hegemony, they court-tributed the Baiyue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chu hegemony the Hundred Yue sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 秦并天下，威服蠻夷，始开领外，置南海、桂林、象郡。

translations.literal: Qin annexed all under Heaven; awed and submitted Man and Yi; first opened beyond the pale; established Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's unification pushed south with Nanhai, Guilin, and Xiang commanderies beyond the old frontier.

sentences.zh: 漢興，尉佗自立為南越王，传國五世。

translations.literal: When Han rose, Wei Tuo established himself as king of Nanyue; the state passed five generations.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han saw Zhao Tuo style himself king of Nuyue through five reigns.

sentences.zh: 至武帝元鼎五年，遂灭之，分置九郡，交阯刺史领焉。

translations.literal: By Emperor Wu's Yuanding fifth year, they then destroyed it; divided and set nine commanderies; Jiaozhi inspector oversaw them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu extinguished Nuyue in 112 B.C.E., carved nine southern commanderies, and placed them under a Jiaozhi inspector.

sentences.zh: 其珠崖、儋耳二郡在海洲上，东西千里，南北五百里。

translations.literal: Its Zhuya and Dan'er two commanderies were on sea islets; east-west a thousand li; north-south five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuya and Dan'er covered island chains roughly a thousand li by five hundred.

sentences.zh: 其渠帅貴长耳，皆穿而缒之，垂肩三寸。

translations.literal: Their channel leaders esteemed long ears; all pierced and hung them; dangling past shoulder three cun.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs pierced elongated lobes weighted to hang three inches past the shoulders.

sentences.zh: 武帝末，珠崖太守会稽孫幸调廣幅布献之，蠻不堪役，遂攻郡殺幸。

translations.literal: At Emperor Wu's end, Zhuya governor Kuaiji Sun Xing levied wide-width cloth to present them; the Man could not bear the service; thereupon attacked the commandery and killed Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Sun Xing's cloth levy for Han tribute drove the isles to revolt and kill him.

sentences.zh: 幸子豹合率善人还，復破之，自领郡事，討擊余党，連年乃平。

translations.literal: Xing's son Bao gathered and led good men back; again defeated them; personally oversaw commandery affairs; campaigned and struck remnant factions; successive years before pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bao rallied loyalists, routed the rebels, governed in his father's stead, and spent years mopping up.

sentences.zh: 豹遣使封还印绶，上書言状，制詔即以豹為珠崖太守。

translations.literal: Bao dispatched envoys to seal and return seal-cords; submitted memorial stating the situation; regulated edict thereupon made Bao Zhuya governor.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bao returned the seals with a full report; the court confirmed him as governor.

sentences.zh: 威政大行，献命岁至。

translations.literal: Awesome governance greatly practiced; tribute missions yearly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: His stern rule restored annual tribute from the isles.

sentences.zh: 中國贪其珍赂，漸相侵侮，故率數岁一反。

translations.literal: The Central States coveted their rare bribes; gradually mutually encroached and insulted; therefore generally every few years once rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Han greed for pearls bred exploitation and revolts every few years.

sentences.zh: 元帝初元三年，遂罢之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan's Chuyuan third year—thereupon abolished them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan abolished the commanderies in 46 B.C.E.

sentences.zh: 凡立郡六十五岁。

translations.literal: In all the commanderies stood sixty-five years.
translations.idiomatic: They had lasted sixty-five years.

sentences.zh: 逮王莽輔政，元始二年，日南之南黄支國来献犀牛。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang assisted government, Yuanshi second year, south of Rinan Huangzhi state came and presented a rhinoceros.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang's regency brought a rhino gift from Huangzhi beyond Rinan.

sentences.zh: 凡交阯所统，雖置郡縣，而言語各异，重譯乃通。

translations.literal: In all Jiaozhi's oversight, although commanderies and counties were set, speech and language each differed; repeated interpreting then communicated.
translations.idiomatic: Despite county administration, languages required chained interpreters.

sentences.zh: 人如禽兽，长幼無别。

translations.literal: People were like birds and beasts; elder and young had no distinction.
translations.idiomatic: People lived like animals, without order between old and young.

sentences.zh: 项髻徒跣，以布贯頭而著之。

translations.literal: Topknots in chignons, bare feet; they used cloth to thread the head and wear it.
translations.idiomatic: They went barefoot with chignons and cloth slipped over the head like a poncho.

sentences.zh: 后颇徙中國罪人，使杂居其間，乃稍知言語，漸见礼化。

translations.literal: Later they somewhat exiled Central States convicts, caused them to dwell mixed among them; then they gradually knew speech; gradually saw ritual transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Settled Chinese convicts spread the language and a little civilizing ritual.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，锡光為交阯，任延守九真，于是教其耕稼，制為冠履，初設媒娉，始知姻娶，建立学校，导之礼義。

translations.literal: At Guangwu's restoration, Xi Guang was Jiaozhi, Ren Yan guarded Jiuzhen; thereupon he taught them plow and plant; regulated caps and shoes; first set go-betweens and betrothal; first knew marriage taking; established schools; guided them in ritual and rightness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu's officials Xi Guang and Ren Yan brought farming, shoes, betrothal rites, schools, and moral instruction to Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 建武十二年，九真徼外蠻里張游，率种人慕化内屬，封為歸漢里君。

translations.literal: Jianwu twelfth year, beyond the pale of Jiuzhen Man village Zhang You led tribal kind to admire transformation and submit internally; enfeoffed as lord of Gui-Han village.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 36: Zhang You of outer Jiuzhen brought his people to allegiance and became Han's "lord of the Submit-to-Han hamlet."

sentences.zh: 明年，南越徼外蠻夷献白雉、白菟。

translations.literal: The next year, beyond the pale of Nanyue Man and Yi presented white pheasant and white hare.
translations.idiomatic: The following year southern frontier tribes offered white pheasants and hares.

sentences.zh: 至十六年，交阯女子徵側及其妹徵贰反，攻郡。

translations.literal: By the sixteenth year, Jiaozhi woman Zheng Ce and her younger sister Zheng Er rebelled; attacked the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 40: the sisters Zheng Ce and Zheng Er of Jiaozhi rose against the commandery.

sentences.zh: 徵側者，麊泠縣雒將之女也。

translations.literal: Zheng Ce was Mi [-ling] county Luo chief's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ce was daughter of a Luo chief in Mi[-ling] county.

sentences.zh: 嫁為硃珪人詩索妻，甚雄勇。

translations.literal: Married as Zhugui man Shi Suo's wife; very fierce and brave.
translations.idiomatic: Married to Shi Suo of Zhugui, she was famously fierce.

sentences.zh: 交阯太守苏定以法绳之，側忿，故反。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi governor Su Ding used law to cord her; Ce resented; therefore rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Su Ding prosecuted her by Han law; rage sparked the revolt.

sentences.zh: 于是九真、日南、合浦蠻里皆应之，凡略六十五城，自立為王。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiuzhen, Rinan, Hepu Man villages all responded to them; in all they seized sixty-five cities; established themselves as kings.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuzhen, Rinan, and Hepu villages rose with them, took sixty-five towns, and crowned Zheng Ce queen.

sentences.zh: 交阯刺史及諸太守仅得自守。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi inspector and various governors barely could defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Han officials could barely hold their walls.

sentences.zh: 光武乃詔长沙、合浦、交阯具车船，修道桥，通障谿，储粮谷。

translations.literal: Guangwu thereupon ordered Changsha, Hepu, Jiaozhi to prepare carts and boats, repair roads and bridges, penetrate barrier streams, store grain.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu mobilized boats, roads, bridges, and grain across the southern commanderies.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遣伏波將軍馬援、楼船將軍段志，发长沙、桂阳、零陵、苍梧兵萬余人討之。

translations.literal: Eighteenth year, dispatched General Fubo Ma Yuan, tower-ship general Duan Zhi; mobilized Changsha, Guiyang, Lingling, Cangwu troops more than ten thousand to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 42: Ma Yuan and Duan Zhi led ten thousand southern troops against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 明年夏四月，援破交阯，斬徵側、徵贰等，余皆降散。

translations.literal: Next year summer fourth month, Yuan broke Jiaozhi; beheaded Zheng Ce, Zheng Er, and others; the rest all surrendered and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer Ma Yuan took Jiaozhi, executed both sisters, and dispersed their armies.

sentences.zh: 進擊九真贼都阳等，破降之。

translations.literal: Advanced to strike Jiuzhen bandits Du Yang and others; defeated and made them surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed into Jiuzhen and crushed Du Yang's holdouts.

sentences.zh: 徙其渠帅三百余口于零陵。

translations.literal: Moved their channel leaders more than three hundred persons to Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred rebel chiefs were resettled in Lingling.

sentences.zh: 于是领表悉平。

translations.literal: Thereupon south of the ridge all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The southern frontier was quiet again.

sentences.zh: 肃宗元和元年，日南徼外蠻夷究不事人邑豪献生犀、白雉。

translations.literal: Suzong Yuanhe first year, beyond Rinan Man and Yi Jiubushi people's settlement chief presented live rhinoceros and white pheasant.
translations.idiomatic: 84 C.E.: Jiubushi headmen beyond Rinan sent a live rhino and white pheasants.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元十二年夏四月，日南、象林蠻夷二千余人寇掠百姓，燔烧官寺，郡縣发兵討擊，斬其渠帅，余众乃降。

translations.literal: Emperor He's Yongyuan twelfth year summer fourth month, Rinan and Xianglin Man and Yi more than two thousand persons raided and plundered common people; burned official temples; commanderies and counties raised troops to strike; beheaded their channel leaders; remaining crowds then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: 100 C.E.: two thousand Rinan and Xianglin tribesmen burned offices until county troops slew their chiefs and accepted surrender.

sentences.zh: 于是置象林將兵长史，以防其患。

translations.literal: Thereupon they set Xianglin commanding troops senior clerk to guard against their peril.
translations.idiomatic: Han created a military overseer at Xianglin to deter further raids.

sentences.zh: 安帝永初元年，九真徼外夜郎蠻夷舉土内屬，开境千八百四十里。

translations.literal: Emperor An's Yongchu first year, beyond Jiuzhen Yelang Man and Yi raised land and submitted internally; opened border one thousand eight hundred forty li.
translations.idiomatic: 107 C.E.: outer Jiuzhen Yelang tribes yielded territory extending Han sway 1,840 li.

sentences.zh: 元初二年，苍梧蠻夷反叛。

translations.literal: Yuanchu second year, Cangwu Man and Yi rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: 115 C.E.: Cangwu tribes rebelled.

sentences.zh: 明年，遂招誘郁林、合浦蠻漢數千人攻苍梧郡。

translations.literal: The next year, thereupon enticed Yulin and Hepu Man and Han several thousand persons to attack Cangwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: They drew thousands from Yulin and Hepu against Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 邓太后遣侍御史任逴奉詔赦之，贼皆降散。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Deng dispatched attendant censor Ren Cong bearing edict to amnesty them; bandits all surrendered and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Deng's amnesty envoys led by Ren Cong broke up the rising.

sentences.zh: 延光元年，九真徼外蠻贡献内屬。

translations.literal: Yanguang first year, beyond Jiuzhen Man presented tribute and submitted internally.
translations.idiomatic: 122 C.E.: outer Jiuzhen tribes submitted with tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年，日南徼外蠻復来内屬。

translations.literal: Third year, beyond Rinan Man again came to submit internally.
translations.idiomatic: 124 C.E.: another wave beyond Rinan yielded allegiance.

sentences.zh: 顺帝永建六年，日南徼外叶调王便遣使贡献，帝賜便金印紫绶。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun's Yongjian sixth year, beyond Rinan Yediao king Bian dispatched envoys with tribute; emperor bestowed on Bian gold seal purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: 131 C.E.: King Bian of Yediao sent tribute; Emperor Shun granted him a gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 永和二年，日南、象林徼外蠻夷区怜等數千人攻象林縣，烧城寺，殺长吏。

translations.literal: Yonghe second year, beyond Rinan and Xianglin Man and Yi Ou Lian and others several thousand persons attacked Xianglin county; burned city temples; killed senior officials.
translations.idiomatic: 137 C.E.: Ou Lian led thousands from beyond Rinan and Xianglin to burn Xianglin and murder officials.

sentences.zh: 交阯刺史樊演发交阯、九真二郡兵萬余人救之。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi inspector Fan Yan mobilized Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen two commanderies' troops more than ten thousand to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Fan Yan raised ten thousand men from Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 兵士惮遠役，遂反，攻其府。

translations.literal: Soldiers feared distant service; thereupon rebelled; attacked their headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The troops mutinied rather than march south and stormed headquarters.

sentences.zh: 二郡雖擊破反者，而贼势转盛。

translations.literal: The two commanderies although struck and broke the rebels, yet bandit power turned stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Both counties crushed the mutiny yet the tribal revolt grew.

sentences.zh: 会侍御史贾昌使在日南，即与州郡并力討之，不利，遂為所攻。

translations.literal: It happened attendant censor Jia Chang was envoy at Rinan; immediately with province and commanderies combined strength campaigned against them; did not prevail; thereupon was attacked by them.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jia Chang joined provincial troops but lost ground and was besieged.

sentences.zh: 围岁余而兵谷不继，帝以為忧。

translations.literal: Besieged more than a year yet troops and grain did not continue; emperor took it as worry.
translations.idiomatic: After a year-long siege supplies failed and the court worried.

sentences.zh: 明年，召公卿百官及四府掾屬，问其方略，皆議遣大將，发荆、杨、兗、豫四萬人赴之。

translations.literal: The next year, summoned dukes, ministers, hundred officials and four offices clerks; asked their stratagems; all debated dispatching a great general; mobilize Jing, Yang, Yan, Yu forty thousand persons to go there.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the court debated sending forty thousand men from four provinces under a senior general.

sentences.zh: 大將軍从事中郎李固驳曰：

translations.literal: General-in-chief staff attendant Li Gu refuted, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Staff adviser Li Gu objected:

sentences.zh: 若荆、杨無事，发之可也。

translations.literal: If Jing and Yang have no troubles, dispatching them is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: If Jing and Yang were quiet, a levy would be fine."

sentences.zh: 今二州盗贼槃結不散，武陵、南郡蠻夷未辑，长沙、桂阳數被征发，如復扰动，必更生患。

translations.literal: Now the two provinces' bandits coil knotted and do not disperse; Wuling and Nan commandery Man and Yi are not collected; Changsha and Guiyang repeatedly suffer levy drafts—if again disturbed, must again produce peril.
translations.idiomatic: But bandits choke those provinces, southern tribes smolder, and Changsha and Guiyang are exhausted—another draft risks fresh disaster."

sentences.zh: 其不可一也。

translations.literal: This is the first unacceptability.
translations.idiomatic: First objection."

sentences.zh: 又兗、豫之人卒被征发，遠赴萬里，無有还期，詔書迫促，必致叛亡。

translations.literal: Also Yan and Yu's people suddenly suffer levy drafts; go far ten thousand li; have no return date; edicts press urgently—must bring desertion and flight.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Yu peasants marched ten thousand li with no return date under harsh orders would desert."

sentences.zh: 其不可二也。

translations.literal: This is the second unacceptability.
translations.idiomatic: Second objection."

sentences.zh: 南州水土温暑，加有瘴气，致死亡者十必四五。

translations.literal: Southern provinces' water and soil are warm and hot; moreover there is miasma qi—those who die reach ten must be four or five.
translations.idiomatic: Southern heat and miasma would kill four or five of every ten men."

sentences.zh: 其不可三也。

translations.literal: This is the third unacceptability.
translations.idiomatic: Third objection."

sentences.zh: 遠涉萬里，士卒疲劳，比至领南，不復堪斗。

translations.literal: Far ford ten thousand li; soldiers and troops weary; by the time reaching south of the ridge, no longer able to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Men would arrive too exhausted to fight after crossing China."

sentences.zh: 其不可四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth unacceptability.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth objection."

sentences.zh: 軍行三十里為程，而去日南九千余里，三百日乃到，計人禀五升，用米六十萬斛，不計將吏驴馬之食，但負甲自致，费便若此。

translations.literal: Army march thirty li as a stage; but distance to Rinan is more than nine thousand li—three hundred days then arrive; reckon person ration five sheng—uses rice six hundred thousand hu; not reckoning officers clerks donkeys horses food; only bearing armor self-delivered—expense then like this.
translations.idiomatic: Nine thousand li means three hundred marches—six hundred thousand hu of grain before counting animals—cost alone defeats the plan."

sentences.zh: 其不可五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth unacceptability.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth objection."

sentences.zh: 設軍到所在，死亡必众，既不足御敌，当復更发，此為刻割心腹以补四支。

translations.literal: Suppose troops arrive at place—deaths must be many; already insufficient to resist enemy—should again issue another levy—this is carving and cutting the heart belly to patch four limbs.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy losses would force fresh levies—flaying the heartland to patch the limbs."

sentences.zh: 其不可六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth unacceptability.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth objection."

sentences.zh: 九真、日南相去千里，发其吏民，犹尚不堪，何况乃苦四州之卒，以赴萬里之艰哉！

translations.literal: Jiuzhen and Rinan apart a thousand li—draft their clerks and people—still not bearable—how much more then afflict four provinces' soldiers to go ten thousand li hardship!
translations.idiomatic: Local Jiuzhen-Rinan levies already buckle—how burden four distant provinces?"

sentences.zh: 其不可七也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh unacceptability.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh objection."

sentences.zh: 前中郎將尹就討益州叛羌，益州谚曰：“虏来尚可，尹来殺我。

translations.literal: Former general of the Gentlemen of the Household Yin Jiu campaigned against Yizhou rebel Qiang; Yizhou proverb says: "When barbarians come still tolerable; when Yin comes he kills us.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou still remembers Yin Jiu's campaign—"Better meet barbarians than Yin Jiu."

sentences.zh: ”后就征还，以兵付刺史張乔。

translations.literal: "Later Jiu was summoned back; handed troops to inspector Zhang Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Recall Yin and give troops to Inspector Zhang Qiao instead."

sentences.zh: 乔因其將吏，旬月之間，破殄寇虏。

translations.literal: Qiao relied on his generals and clerks; within ten-day months, broke and exterminated bandit barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiao crushed the rebels within weeks using local forces."

sentences.zh: 此发將無益之效，州郡可任之验也。

translations.literal: This is proof that dispatching generals has no benefit effect; province and commanderies can be trusted proof.
translations.idiomatic: Proof that central generals waste effort while local leaders succeed."

sentences.zh: 宜更选有勇略仁惠任將帅者，以為刺史、太守，悉使共住交阯。

translations.literal: It is fitting again to select those who have courage, strategy, benevolence, kindness, capable of generalship—make them inspectors and governors; all cause them together to dwell Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint bold, humane men as southern governors and base them in Jiaozhi."

sentences.zh: 今日南兵单無谷，守既不足，戰又不能。

translations.literal: Now Rinan troops are thin and without grain; guard already insufficient; battle moreover cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Rinan lacks troops and grain—cannot hold or strike."

sentences.zh: 可一切徙其吏民，北依交阯，事静之后，又命歸本。

translations.literal: Can altogether relocate their clerks and people north to rely on Jiaozhi; after affairs quiet, again order return to roots.
translations.idiomatic: Evacuate civilians north into Jiaozhi until calm, then send them home."

sentences.zh: 还募蠻夷，使自相攻，转輸金帛，以為其資。

translations.literal: Also recruit Man and Yi; cause them mutually to attack; transport gold and silk to be their resources.
translations.idiomatic: Hire tribal allies to fight each other and fund them with treasure."

sentences.zh: 有能反間致頭首者，許以封侯列士之赏。

translations.literal: Those able to counter-espionage bring heads—promise them enfeoffment marquis lieutenant scholar rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Offer noble rank for defectors who deliver rebel heads."

sentences.zh: 故并州刺史长沙祝良，性多勇决，又南阳張乔，前在益州有破虏之功，皆可任用。

translations.literal: Former Bingzhou inspector Changsha Zhu Liang—nature much brave and decisive; also Nanyang Zhang Qiao—before in Yizhou had merit breaking barbarians—all can be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Liang of Changsha and Zhang Qiao of Nanyang—both proved themselves against barbarians—deserve appointment."

sentences.zh: 昔太宗就加魏尚為云中守，哀帝即拜龚舍為太山太守。

translations.literal: In antiquity Taizong on the spot added Wei Shang as Yunzhong governor; Emperor Ai immediately invested Gong She as Taishan governor.
translations.idiomatic: Like Emperor Wen promoting Wei Shang on the spot or Emperor Ai naming Gong She—act decisively."

sentences.zh: 宜即拜良等，便道之官。

translations.literal: It is fitting immediately invest Liang and others; by convenient route go to office.
translations.idiomatic: Commission Zhu Liang and Zhang Qiao immediately by fast relay."

sentences.zh: 四府悉从固議，即拜祝良為九真太守，張乔為交阯刺史。

translations.literal: Four offices all followed Li Gu's proposal; immediately invested Zhu Liang as Jiuzhen governor; Zhang Qiao as Jiaozhi inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers adopted Li Gu's plan and named Zhu Liang governor of Jiuzhen and Zhang Qiao inspector of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 乔至，开示慰誘，并皆降散。

translations.literal: When Qiao arrived, he opened display and comforted and enticed; together all surrendered and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiao's reassurances dissolved the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 良到九真，单车入贼中，設方略，招以威信，降者數萬人，皆為良筑起府寺。

translations.literal: When Liang arrived at Jiuzhen, single cart entered among bandits; set stratagems; summoned with awe and trust; surrenderers numbered tens of thousands—all for Liang raised and built headquarters temples.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Liang rode alone into rebel ranks and won tens of thousands who built him yamen halls.

sentences.zh: 由是岭外復平。

translations.literal: From this beyond the mountains again was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Peace returned south of the ranges.

sentences.zh: 建康元年，日南蠻夷千余人復攻烧縣邑，遂扇动九真，与相連結。

translations.literal: Jiankang first year, Rinan Man and Yi more than a thousand persons again attacked and burned counties and settlements; thereupon fanned Jiuzhen; mutually linked and joined.
translations.idiomatic: 144 C.E.: over a thousand Rinan tribesmen burned towns and stirred Jiuzhen into alliance.

sentences.zh: 交阯刺史九江夏方开恩招誘，贼皆降服。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi inspector Jiujiang Xia Fang opened grace and summoned and enticed; bandits all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Xia Fang of Jiujiang talked them down.

sentences.zh: 時梁太后临朝，美方之功，迁為桂阳太守。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Liang faced court; admired Fang's merit; transferred him to be Guiyang governor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Liang rewarded Xia Fang with Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 桓帝永寿二年，居風令贪暴無度，縣人硃达等及蠻夷相聚，攻殺縣令，众至四五千人，進攻九真，九真太守□式戰死。

translations.literal: Emperor Huan's Yongshou second year, Jufeng magistrate was greedy and cruel without limit; county people Zhu Da and others together with Man and Yi gathered; attacked and killed the magistrate; crowds reached four or five thousand persons; advanced attacked Jiuzhen; Jiuzhen governor □ Shi died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: 156 C.E.: a rapacious Jufeng magistrate sparked Zhu Da's rising—four or five thousand tribesmen killed the prefect and stormed Jiuzhen; Governor Shi fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 詔賜钱六十萬，拜子二人為郎。

translations.literal: Edict bestowed six hundred thousand cash; appointed two sons gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted six hundred thousand cash and two sons posts as gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 遣九真都尉魏朗討破之，斬首二千級，渠帅犹屯据日南，众转强盛。

translations.literal: Dispatched Jiuzhen commandant Wei Lang to campaign and break them; beheaded two thousand grades; channel leaders still massed and occupied Rinan; crowds turned stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Wei Lang took two thousand heads yet chiefs still held Rinan and grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 延熹三年，詔復拜夏方為交阯刺史。

translations.literal: Yanxi third year, edict again invested Xia Fang as Jiaozhi inspector.
translations.idiomatic: 160 C.E.: Xia Fang returned as Jiaozhi inspector.

sentences.zh: 方威惠素著，日南宿贼聞之，二萬余人相率诣方降。

translations.literal: Fang's awe and grace was long manifest; Rinan long-standing bandits heard it; more than twenty thousand persons together led one another to Fang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand veteran rebels surrendered to Xia Fang's reputation.

sentences.zh: 靈帝建宁三年，郁林太守谷永以恩信招降烏滸人十余萬内屬，皆受冠带，开置七縣。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling's Jianning third year, Yulin governor Gu Yong with grace and trust summoned and surrendered Wuhu people more than one hundred thousand internally submitted; all received caps and belts; opened and set seven counties.
translations.idiomatic: 170 C.E.: Gu Yong of Yulin enrolled over one hundred thousand Wuhu under Han registration across seven new counties.

sentences.zh: 熹平二年冬十二月，日南徼外國重譯贡献。

translations.literal: Xiping second year winter twelfth month, beyond Rinan foreign states repeated interpreter tribute.
translations.idiomatic: December 173 C.E.: relay envoys from beyond Rinan brought tribute.

sentences.zh: 光和元年，交阯、合浦烏滸蠻反叛，招誘九真、日南，合數萬人，攻没郡縣。

translations.literal: Guanghe first year, Jiaozhi and Hepu Wuhu Man rebelled; enticed Jiuzhen and Rinan; combined several tens of thousands; attacked and drowned commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: 178 C.E.: Wuhu tribes in Jiaozhi and Hepu drew Jiuzhen and Rinan into a rising that overran counties.

sentences.zh: 四年，刺史硃俊擊破之。

translations.literal: Fourth year, inspector Zhu Jun attacked and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: 181 C.E.: Inspector Zhu Jun crushed them.

sentences.zh: 六年，日南徼外國復来贡献。

translations.literal: Sixth year, beyond Rinan foreign states again came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: 183 C.E.: overseas kingdoms beyond Rinan resumed tribute.

sentences.zh: 巴郡南郡蠻，本有五姓：巴氏、樊氏、瞫氏，相氏，郑氏。

translations.literal: Ba commandery and Nan commandery Man originally had five surnames: the Ba, Fan, Shen, Xiang, and Zheng clans.
translations.idiomatic: The Ba and Nan commandery tribes trace five clans: Ba, Fan, Shen, Xiang, and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 皆出于武落钟離山。

translations.literal: All came out from Mount Wuluo Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: All five claimed descent from Mount Wuluo Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 其山有赤黑二穴，巴氏之子生于赤穴，四姓之子皆生黑穴。

translations.literal: That mountain has red and black two caves; the Ba clan's sons were born in the red cave; the four surnames' sons were all born in the black caves.
translations.idiomatic: Two caves—red and black—yielded the Ba line from the crimson grotto and the other four from the black.

sentences.zh: 未有君长，俱事鬼神，乃共掷剑于石穴，约能中者，奉以為君。

translations.literal: They had no ruler; all served ghosts and spirits; then together cast swords at the stone cave; they covenanted—whoever could hit would be honored as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: With no chief, they turned to divination: whoever drove a sword into the cave rock would lead.

sentences.zh: 巴氏子务相乃獨中之，众皆叹。

translations.literal: Ba clan's son Wuxiang then alone hit it; all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wuxiang of the Ba clan struck true; the rest acclaimed him.

sentences.zh: 又令各乘土船，约能浮者，当以為君。

translations.literal: Again they ordered each to ride earthen boats; they covenanted—whoever could float should be made ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Next they raced clay boats—whoever stayed afloat would rule.

sentences.zh: 余姓悉沉，唯务相獨浮。

translations.literal: The remaining surnames all sank; only Wuxiang alone floated.
translations.idiomatic: The rival clans sank; Wuxiang alone rode high.

sentences.zh: 因共立之，是為廪君。

translations.literal: Thereupon together they established him; this is Lord Lin.
translations.idiomatic: They enthroned him as Lord Lin, the Granary Lord.

sentences.zh: 乃乘土船，从夷水至鹽阳。

translations.literal: Then riding earthen boats, from Yishui they reached Yanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed the Yishui downstream to Yanyang.

sentences.zh: 鹽水有神女，謂廪君曰：“此地廣大，鱼鹽所出，愿留共居。

translations.literal: The brine had a goddess who said to Lord Lin, ‘This country is wide, and fish and salt come from it; I wish you would stay and live with me here.’
translations.idiomatic: A goddess of the salt flats asked Lord Lin to share her bountiful domain.

sentences.zh: ”廪君不許。

translations.literal: Lord Lin would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Lin refused.

sentences.zh: 鹽神暮輒来取宿，旦即化為虫，与諸虫群飞，掩蔽日光，天地晦冥。

translations.literal: The salt goddess at dusk always came to take lodging; at dawn then transformed into an insect; with various insects flew in swarms; veiled and blocked sunlight; heaven and earth dark and dim.
translations.idiomatic: Each dusk she shared his bed; each dawn she became a cloud of insects that eclipsed the sun.

sentences.zh: 积十余日，廪君伺其便，因射殺之，天乃开明。

translations.literal: Accumulated more than ten days; Lord Lin watched for his chance; thereupon shot and killed her; heaven then opened bright.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days of gloom he shot her at an opening; daylight returned.

sentences.zh: 廪君于是君乎夷城，四姓皆臣之。

translations.literal: Lord Lin thereupon ruled as lord at Yicheng; the four surnames all became his subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Lin founded his seat at Yicheng and the four clans submitted.

sentences.zh: 廪君死，魂魄世為白虎。

translations.literal: When Lord Lin died, his hun and po for generations became a white tiger.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit passed down as a white tiger.

sentences.zh: 巴氏以虎饮人血，遂以人祠焉。

translations.literal: The Ba clan because the tiger drank human blood, thereupon used humans to sacrifice to it.
translations.idiomatic: The Ba fed the tiger spirit with human blood offerings.

sentences.zh: 及秦惠王并巴中，以巴氏以蠻夷君长，世尚秦女，其民爵比不更，有罪得以爵除。

translations.literal: When King Hui of Qin annexed central Ba, he took the Ba clan as Man-Yi chiefs, generation after generation married Qin women; their people's rank compared to bugeng; having guilt could use rank to remit.
translations.idiomatic: King Hui of Qin enrolled the Ba as hereditary chiefs married to Qin princesses; commoners held bugeng-equivalent rank and could commute crimes with rank.

sentences.zh: 其君长岁出赋二千一十六钱，三岁一出義赋千八百钱。

translations.literal: Their chiefs yearly paid tax two thousand sixteen cash; every third year paid once yi-tax one thousand eight hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs paid 2,016 cash yearly and a special levy of 1,800 every third year.

sentences.zh: 其民户出幏布八丈二尺，鸡羽三十鍭。

translations.literal: Their common households issued jia cloth eight zhang two chi; chicken feathers thirty hou.
translations.idiomatic: Households owed eight zhang two of tribute cloth and thirty bundles of feathers.

sentences.zh: 漢興，南郡太守靳强請一依秦時故事。

translations.literal: When Han rose, Nan commandery governor Jin Qiang requested entirely to follow Qin times' precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han's Governor Jin Qiang of Nan asked to keep Qin-era arrangements.

sentences.zh: 至建武二十三年，南郡潳山蠻雷迁等始反叛，寇掠百姓，遣武威將軍劉尚將萬余人討破之，徙其种人七千余口置江夏界中，今沔中蠻是也。

translations.literal: By Jianwu twenty-third year, Nan commandery Tushan Man Lei Qian and others first rebelled; raided and plundered common people; dispatched General Weiwu Liu Shang leading more than ten thousand to campaign and break them; relocated their tribal kind more than seven thousand persons and placed them in Jiangxia border; today's Han-river Man are these.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwu 47: Lei Qian of Tushan revolted until Liu Shang crushed the rising; seven thousand captives were moved into Jiangxia—the ancestors of the Han-river Man.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元十三年，巫蠻許圣等以郡收税不均，怀怨恨，遂屯聚反叛。

translations.literal: Emperor He's Yongyuan thirteenth year, Wu Man Xu Sheng and others because the commandery collected taxes unevenly harbored resentment; thereupon gathered and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: 101 C.E.: Xu Sheng's Wu tribes rose over unfair assessments.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，遣使者督荆州諸郡兵萬余人討之。

translations.literal: The next summer, dispatched envoys to supervise Jingzhou various commanderies' troops more than ten thousand to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Next summer envoys led ten thousand Jingzhou troops against them.

sentences.zh: 圣等依凭阻隘，久不破。

translations.literal: Sheng and others relied on perilous narrows; long not broken.
translations.idiomatic: They held the defiles for months.

sentences.zh: 諸軍乃分道并進，或自巴郡、鱼復數路攻之，蠻乃散走，斬其渠帅。

translations.literal: The various armies then divided roads and advanced together; some from Ba commandery and Yufu several routes attacked them; the Man then scattered and fled; beheaded their channel leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Han columns converged from Ba and Yufu, routed the tribes, and slew their chiefs.

sentences.zh: 乘胜追之，大破圣等。

translations.literal: Riding victory they pursued them; greatly defeated Sheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit shattered Xu Sheng's force.

sentences.zh: 圣等乞降，復悉徙置江夏。

translations.literal: Sheng and others begged to surrender; again entirely relocated and placed in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: They surrendered and were resettled again in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 靈帝建宁二年，江夏蠻叛，州郡討平之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling's Jianning second year, Jiangxia Man rebelled; province and commandery campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: 169 C.E.: Jiangxia tribes rose and were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 光和三年，江夏蠻復反，与庐江贼黄穰相連結，十余萬人，攻没四縣，寇患累年。

translations.literal: Guanghe third year, Jiangxia Man again rebelled; linked with Lujiang bandit Huang Rang; more than one hundred thousand persons; attacked and drowned four counties; raid peril successive years.
translations.idiomatic: 180 C.E.: Jiangxia tribes joined Huang Rang's hundred-thousand host and held four counties for years.

sentences.zh: 庐江太守陆康討破之，余悉降散。

translations.literal: Lujiang governor Lu Kang campaigned and broke them; remainder all surrendered and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang of Lujiang broke the coalition and dispersed the rest.

sentences.zh: 板楯蠻夷者，秦昭襄王時，有一白虎，常从群虎數游秦、蜀、巴、漢之境，伤害千余人。

translations.literal: As for the shield-board Man and Yi: in the time of King Zhaoxiang of Qin there was a white tiger that often ranged with packs of tigers back and forth across Qin, Shu, Ba, and Han, killing or wounding more than a thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: The shield-board tribes: under King Zhaoxiang of Qin a white tiger roamed Qin, Shu, Ba, and Han with a pride and killed over a thousand people.

sentences.zh: 昭王乃重募國中有能殺虎者，赏邑萬家，金百镒。

translations.literal: King Zhaoxiang then offered rich rewards across the state for anyone who could kill the tiger, promising a fief of ten thousand households and one hundred yi of gold.
translations.idiomatic: The king posted a huge bounty—a ten-thousand-household fief and a hundred yi of gold—for the tiger’s head.

sentences.zh: 時，有巴郡阆中夷人，能作白竹之弩，乃登楼射殺白虎。

translations.literal: At that time there was a Yi man from Langzhong in Ba commandery who could craft white-bamboo crossbows; he climbed a tower and shot the white tiger dead.
translations.idiomatic: A Langzhong tribesman built white-bamboo crossbows, took a high vantage, and slew the beast.

sentences.zh: 昭王嘉之，而以其夷人，不欲加封，乃刻石盟要，復夷人顷田不租，十妻不算，伤人者论，殺人者得以□钱赎死。

translations.literal: King Zhaoxiang commended him but, because he was a Yi, declined to ennoble him; instead he carved a covenant in stone with its essential terms: Yi grain land measured in qing would again pay no rent; ten wives would not be counted for tax; those who injured others would be sentenced according to law; those who killed others could redeem execution with an indemnity in cash.
translations.idiomatic: The king honored him but withheld a Chinese noble title, recording instead a stone pact: rent-free fields, extra wives exempt from head tax, standard penalties for wounding, and commutation of execution for homicide by cash payment.

sentences.zh: 盟曰：“秦犯夷，輸黄龍一双；

translations.literal: The covenant read: ‘If Qin wrongs the Yi, let Qin deliver a pair of yellow dragons;
translations.idiomatic: The treaty ran: if Qin broke faith with the tribes, Qin owed a pair of yellow dragons.

sentences.zh: 夷犯秦，輸清酒一钟。

translations.literal: if the Yi wrong Qin, let the Yi deliver one zhong of clear wine.’
translations.idiomatic: If the tribes wronged Qin, they owed a jar of clear wine.

sentences.zh: ”夷人安之。

translations.literal: The Yi accepted this arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes found the terms acceptable.

sentences.zh: 至高祖為漢王，发夷人还伐三秦。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became King of Han, he mobilized the Yi tribesmen and sent them back to campaign against the Three Qins.
translations.idiomatic: As King of Han, Liu Bang drafted the Ba tribesmen for the campaign that broke the Three Qins.

sentences.zh: 秦地既定，乃遣还巴中，復其渠帅罗、朴、督、鄂、度、夕、龚七姓，不輸租赋，余户乃岁入賨钱，口四十。

translations.literal: Once Qin territory was secured, he sent them home to central Ba and restored their seven channel-chief surnames—Luo, Pu, Du, E, Du, Xi, and Gong—who paid no rent or levies; the remaining households paid yearly cong money at forty cash per person.
translations.idiomatic: After the Guanzhong settlement he returned them to Ba, restored the seven hereditary chief lineages tax-free, and taxed everyone else forty cash per capita annually.

sentences.zh: 世号為板楯蠻珍。

translations.literal: For generations they were called the shield-board Man “treasures.”
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth they were prized as the shield-board tribes.

sentences.zh: 阆中有渝水，其人多居水左右，天性劲勇，初為漢前锋，數陷陳。

translations.literal: Langzhong has the Yu River; most of its people dwell along both banks; by nature they are tough and brave; at first they served Han as vanguard and repeatedly broke enemy formations.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Yu in Langzhong lived fierce fighters who spearheaded Han assaults and shattered enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 俗喜歌舞，高祖观之，曰：“此武王伐纣之歌也。

translations.literal: Their custom delighted in song and dance; Gaozu watched and said, “This is the song of King Wu’s campaign against Zhou.”
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu watched their dancing and declared it the martial hymn of King Wu’s war on the Shang.

sentences.zh: ”乃命乐人习之，所謂《巴渝舞》也。

translations.literal: He then ordered musicians to learn it—what is called the Bayu Dance.
translations.idiomatic: Court musicians rehearsed the piece that became the famous Bayu Dance.

sentences.zh: 遂世世服从。

translations.literal: Thereafter generation after generation they submitted and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: They remained loyal subjects for generations.

sentences.zh: 至于中興，郡守常率以征伐。

translations.literal: Down to the restoration, commandery governors often led them on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Han, prefects routinely led them into battle.

sentences.zh: 桓帝之世，板楯數反，太守蜀郡趙温以恩信降服之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Huan’s reign the shield-board tribes rebelled repeatedly; Governor Zhao Wen of Shu commandery pacified them with kindness and good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan’s day saw repeated shield-board revolts until Zhao Wen of Shu won them over by trust.

sentences.zh: 靈帝光和二年，巴郡板楯復叛，寇掠三蜀及漢中諸郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling’s second Guanghe year, the shield-board tribes of Ba commandery rebelled again, raiding the three Shu regions and the Hanzhong commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: 179 C.E.: Ba’s shield-board warriors swept Shu and Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 靈帝遣御史中丞萧瑗督益州兵討之，連年不能克。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling sent Imperial Secretary Assistant Xiao Yuan to supervise Yizhou troops against them; year after year he could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yuan’s Yizhou columns stalled for years.

sentences.zh: 帝欲大发兵，乃问益州計吏，考以征討方略。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to mobilize a large army, so he questioned Yizhou’s reporting clerk and examined him on strategy for the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Planning a major surge, the court quizzed Yizhou’s fiscal envoy on how to fight.

sentences.zh: 漢中上計程包对曰：“板楯七姓，射殺白虎，立功先世，復為義人。

translations.literal: Hanzhong’s reporter Cheng Bao replied: “The seven shield-board surnames shot the white tiger and earned merit for earlier generations; they have again proved righteous people.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Bao of Hanzhong answered: ‘Those seven clans slew the white tiger for Qin and have since served in good faith.’

sentences.zh: 其人勇猛，善于兵戰。

translations.literal: Those men are fierce and brave and excel in warfare.
translations.idiomatic: They are veteran fighters.’

sentences.zh: 昔永初中，羌入漢川，郡縣破坏，得板楯救之，羌死败殆尽，故号為神兵。

translations.literal: Formerly in the Yongchu era the Qiang entered the Han river basin; commanderies and counties were ruined; the shield-board tribes rescued the situation; the Qiang died and were defeated almost completely—hence they were called divine troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongchu troubles they crushed the Qiang incursion and earned the name ‘spirit soldiers.’

sentences.zh: 羌人畏忌，传語种辈，勿復南行。

translations.literal: The Qiang feared them and passed word among their tribes not to march south again.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified Qiang riders warned one another not to advance south.

sentences.zh: 至建和二年，羌復大入，實赖板楯連摧破之。

translations.literal: By Jianhe second year the Qiang invaded again in force; it truly depended on the shield-board tribes repeatedly smashing them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang returned in 148, only the shield-board auxiliaries broke their strength.

sentences.zh: 前车骑將軍冯绲，南征武陵，雖受丹阳精兵之锐，亦倚板楯以成其功。

translations.literal: The former General of Chariots and Cavalry Feng Huan, campaigning south against Wuling, though he received the keen edge of Danyang’s crack troops, still relied on the shield-board tribes to complete his success.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Huan’s southern campaign leaned on them even beside Danyang’s elite.

sentences.zh: 近益州郡亂，太守李颙，亦以板楯討而平之。

translations.literal: Recently when Yizhou commandery was in turmoil, Governor Li Yong likewise used the shield-board tribes to campaign and pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong recently used them to crush unrest in Yizhou commandery.

sentences.zh: 忠功如此，本無恶心。

translations.literal: Their loyalty and merit are such—they fundamentally harbor no evil intent.
translations.idiomatic: They have never lacked loyalty.’

sentences.zh: 长吏乡亭，更赋至重，僕役□楚，过于奴虏，亦有嫁妻賣子，或乃至自刭割。

translations.literal: District and township officials impose alternate levies that are extremely heavy; corvée labor and rod punishments are cruel, worse than slavery; some sell wives and children, or even cut their own throats.
translations.idiomatic: Now petty officials bleed them with surcharges and brutal labor—worse than keeping slaves—until families sell kin or take their own lives.’

sentences.zh: 雖陳冤州郡，而牧守不為通理。

translations.literal: Though they present grievances to province and commandery, governors and shepherds do not relay them for justice.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial benches ignore their petitions.’

sentences.zh: 阙庭悠遠，不能自聞。

translations.literal: The palace is distant; they cannot make themselves heard.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is too far for their voices to reach.’

sentences.zh: 含怨呼天，叩心穷谷。

translations.literal: Harboring resentment they cry to Heaven; they beat their breasts in deep valleys.
translations.idiomatic: They curse Heaven in empty ravines.’

sentences.zh: 愁苦赋役，困罹酷刑。

translations.literal: They worry bitterly over taxes and service and suffer cruel punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes, labor, and torture have driven them to despair.’

sentences.zh: 故邑落相聚，以致叛戾。

translations.literal: Therefore hamlets gather together and so produce rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Villages band together and rise—not from ambition.’

sentences.zh: 非有谋主僭号，以图不轨。

translations.literal: They have no scheming leader usurping titles to plot treason.
translations.idiomatic: No pretender leads them; they seek relief, not empire.’

sentences.zh: 今但选明能牧守，自然安集，不烦征伐也。

translations.literal: Now if we simply select wise and capable governors and shepherds, they will naturally settle and gather—there is no need to trouble with campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint honest prefects and they will quiet down without another expedition.’

sentences.zh: ”帝从其言，遣太守曹谦宣詔赦之，即皆降服。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his words, dispatched Governor Cao Qian to proclaim an edict pardoning them, and immediately all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed; Cao Qian’s amnesty brought instant submission.

sentences.zh: 至中平五年，巴郡黄巾贼起，板楯蠻夷因此復叛，寇掠城邑，遣西園上軍别部司馬趙瑾討平之。

translations.literal: By Zhongping fifth year, Yellow Turban bandits arose in Ba commandery; the shield-board Man and Yi therefore rebelled again, raiding cities and towns; the court dispatched Separate Division Major Zhao Jin of the Western Garden Upper Army to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: 188 C.E.: Turban troubles in Ba sparked another shield-board rising until Zhao Jin crushed it.

sentences.zh: 西南夷

translations.literal: The Southwestern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Southwestern Tribes

sentences.zh: 西南夷者，在蜀郡徼外。

translations.literal: As for the Southwestern Yi, they lie beyond Shu commandery’s frontier.
translations.idiomatic: These peoples lived south and west of Shu commandery’s border marches.

sentences.zh: 有夜郎國，东接交阯，西有滇國，北有邛都國，各立君长。

translations.literal: There is the Yelang state; on the east it joins Jiaozhi; to the west is the Dian state; to the north is the Qiongdu state; each established lords and chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Yelang bordered Jiaozhi, Dian lay to its west, Qiongdu to its north—each with its own ruler.

sentences.zh: 其人皆椎結左衽，邑聚而居，能耕田。

translations.literal: Their people all wore hair in mallet-knots and left-lapped robes; they dwelt gathered in settlements and could plow fields.
translations.idiomatic: They wore topknots and left-lapped robes, lived in clustered villages, and farmed.

sentences.zh: 其外又有巂、昆明諸落，西极同師，东北至叶榆，地方數千里。

translations.literal: Beyond them there were again Xi and Kunming bands; westward they reached Tongshi; northeastward to Yeyu—the territory spans several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond lay Xi and Kunming bands stretching thousands of li from Tongshi west to Yeyu northeast.

sentences.zh: 無君长，辫发，隨畜迁徙無常。

translations.literal: They had no lords or chiefs; they braided hair; following livestock they moved without fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Without chiefs, they braided their hair and followed herds seasonally.

sentences.zh: 自巂东北有莋都國，东北有冉駹國，或土著，或隨畜迁徙。

translations.literal: Northeast from Xi there is the Zuodu state; northeastward there is the Ranmao state—some are settled natives, some follow livestock and move.
translations.idiomatic: Zuodu and Ranmao lay northeast of Xi—some sedentary, some pastoral.

sentences.zh: 自冉駹东北有白馬國，氐种是也。

translations.literal: Northeast from Ranmao there is the White Horse state—they are Di stock.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast of Ranmao stood White Horse Di country.

sentences.zh: 此三國亦有君长。

translations.literal: These three states likewise have lords and chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Those three polities also had recognized rulers.

sentences.zh: 夜郎者，初有女子浣于遁水，有三节大竹流入足間，聞其中有号声，剖竹视之，得一男兒，歸而养之。

translations.literal: As for Yelang: at first a woman was washing in the Dunshui; a great bamboo in three sections floated in between her feet; hearing inside it the sound of crying, she split the bamboo and looked; obtaining a male child, she returned and reared him.
translations.idiomatic: Legend says a washerwoman on the Dun River heard an infant inside a bamboo tube and raised the boy who founded Yelang.

sentences.zh: 及长，有才武，自立為夜郎侯，以竹為姓。

translations.literal: When grown he had talent and martial prowess; he established himself as Marquis of Yelang and took Bamboo as his surname.
translations.idiomatic: He grew into a warrior-king, styled himself Marquis of Yelang, and adopted the surname Zhu (‘bamboo’).

sentences.zh: 武帝元鼎六年，平南夷，為牂柯郡，夜郎侯迎降，天子賜其王印绶。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu’s sixth Yuanding year, he pacified the southern Yi and made Zangke commandery; the Marquis of Yelang came out to surrender; the Son of Heaven bestowed on him the king’s seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In 111 B.C. Han annexed the south as Zangke commandery; the Yelang ruler surrendered and received an imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 后遂殺之。

translations.literal: Later they then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court later executed him.

sentences.zh: 夷獠咸以竹王非血气所生，甚重之，求為立后。

translations.literal: The Yi and Lao all considered the Bamboo King not born of blood and breath; they greatly revered him and requested to establish shrines for him.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribes revered the bamboo-born king as divine and petitioned for cult honors.

sentences.zh: 牂柯太守吳霸以聞，天子乃封其三子為侯。

translations.literal: Zangke Governor Wu Ba reported it; the Son of Heaven then enfeoffed his three sons as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wu Ba relayed the plea; the emperor ennobled the king’s three sons.

sentences.zh: 死，配食其父。

translations.literal: When dead, they received joint sacrifice with their father.
translations.idiomatic: At death they shared altar offerings with their father.

sentences.zh: 今夜郎縣有竹王三郎神是也。

translations.literal: Today Yelang county has the spirits of Bamboo King’s third sons—this is they.
translations.idiomatic: Yelang county still honors the Third Sons of the Bamboo King.

sentences.zh: 初，楚顷襄王時，遣將庄豪从沅水伐夜郎，軍至且兰，椓船于岸而步戰。

translations.literal: At first, in King Qingxiang of Chu’s time, he dispatched general Zhuang Hao to campaign against Yelang along the Yuan River; the army reached Qielan, beached the boats on the bank, and fought on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Chu’s Zhuang Hao sailed the Yuan to Qielan, beached his fleet, and marched inland against Yelang.

sentences.zh: 既灭夜郎，因留王滇池。

translations.literal: After extinguishing Yelang, he therefore remained and ruled Dianchi.
translations.idiomatic: After crushing Yelang he stayed to rule the Dianchi basin.

sentences.zh: 以且兰有椓船牂柯處，乃改其名為牂柯。

translations.literal: Because Qielan had a place for beaching boats at Zangke, they changed its name to Zangke.
translations.idiomatic: Qielan’s boat landing on the Zangke rapids gave the district its new name.

sentences.zh: 牂柯地多雨潦，俗好巫鬼禁忌，寡畜生，又無蚕桑，故其郡最贫。

translations.literal: Zangke land has much rain and flooding; custom esteems shamans, ghosts, and taboos; livestock are few; moreover there is no silkworm mulberry—therefore that commandery is poorest.
translations.idiomatic: Zangke’s rains, spirit cults, few herds, and no sericulture made it Han’s poorest commandery.

sentences.zh: 句町縣有□桹木，可以為面，百姓資之。

translations.literal: Juding county has [missing graph] lang trees whose fruit can serve as grain; common people rely on them.
translations.idiomatic: Juding’s lang fruit sustained the poor as a grain substitute.
