sentences.zh: 公孫述時，大姓龍、傅、尹、董氏，与郡功曹谢暹保境為漢，乃遣使从番禺江奉贡。

translations.literal: In Gongsun Shu’s time the great clans Long, Fu, Yin, and Dong, together with commandery merit clerk Xie Xian, defended the territory for Han; then they dispatched envoys from the Panyu River to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under the warlord Gongsun Shu, leading families and Xie Xian kept Zangke loyal to Han and sent tribute down the Pearl River.

sentences.zh: 光武嘉之，并加褒赏。

translations.literal: Guangwu praised them and moreover added rewards and honors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu rewarded their loyalty handsomely.

sentences.zh: 桓帝時，郡人尹珍自以生于荒裔，不知礼義，乃从汝南許慎、应奉受经書图纬，学成，还乡里教授，于是南域始有学焉。

translations.literal: In Emperor Huan’s time, commandery man Yin Zhen considered himself born on a wild frontier and ignorant of ritual and propriety; thereupon he studied the classics and apocryphal charts with Xu Shen and Ying Feng of Runan; when his learning was complete he returned home and taught—thereupon the southern regions first had scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhen studied under Xu Shen and Ying Feng, then brought classical learning to the far south.

sentences.zh: 珍官至荆州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhen’s office reached Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 滇王者，庄蹻之后也。

translations.literal: The Dian king is descended from Zhuang Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of Dian traced their line to the general Zhuang Qiao.

sentences.zh: 元封二年，武帝平之，以其地為益州郡，割牂柯、越巂各數縣配之。

translations.literal: Second Yuanfeng year, Emperor Wu pacified it and took its territory as Yizhou commandery, carving off several counties each from Zangke and Yuexi to attach to it.
translations.idiomatic: 109 B.C. Han organized Dian as Yizhou commandery, attaching counties from Zangke and Yuexi.

sentences.zh: 后數年，復并昆明地，皆以屬之此郡。

translations.literal: After several years, again annexing Kunming territory, all were attached to this commandery.
translations.idiomatic: A few years later Kunming lands were folded into the same prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有池，周回二百余里，水源深廣，而末更浅狭，有似倒流，故謂之滇池。

translations.literal: There is a lake, circuit more than two hundred li; its water source is deep and broad, yet its outlet becomes shallower and narrower, somewhat like flowing backward—therefore it is called Dian Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Lake Dian spans two hundred li; its deep headwaters taper like a reversed stream—hence the name.

sentences.zh: 河土平敞，多出鹦鹉、孔雀，有鹽池田渔之饶，金銀畜产之富。

translations.literal: The river lands are flat and open; parrots and peacocks abound; there is richness from salt ponds, fields, and fishing; wealth in gold, silver, and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Broad valleys yield parrots and peacocks, salt pans and fisheries, and glittering herds and mines.

sentences.zh: 人俗豪忲。

translations.literal: Among the people custom is proud and extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: The folk were proud and extravagant.

sentences.zh: 居官者皆富及累世。

translations.literal: Those who held office all grew wealthy for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Officeholders grew rich for generations.

sentences.zh: 及王莽政亂，益州郡夷栋蚕、若豆等起兵殺郡守，越巂姑復夷人大牟亦皆叛，殺略吏人。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang’s government fell into chaos, Yizhou commandery Yi Dongcan, Ruoduo, and others raised troops and killed the governor; Yuexi Gufu Yi Damou likewise all rebelled, killing and plundering officials.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Mang’s collapse, Dongcan and Ruoduo slew the Yizhou governor while Damou’s Gufu tribes in Yuexi murdered officials.

sentences.zh: 莽遣宁始將軍廉丹，发巴蜀吏人及转兵谷卒徙十余萬擊之。

translations.literal: Mang dispatched General Who Begins Tranquility Lian Dan, mobilizing Ba-Shu officials and commoners plus grain-transport soldier-settlers numbering more than one hundred thousand to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Mang sent Lian Dan with over a hundred thousand Ba-Shu troops and supply columns.

sentences.zh: 吏士饥疫，連年不能克而还。

translations.literal: Officials and troops suffered hunger and plague; year after year they could not prevail and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hunger and epidemic stalled the campaign until Han withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以廣漢文齐為太守，造起陂池，开通溉灌，垦田二千余顷。

translations.literal: They appointed Guanghan’s Wen Qi as governor; he built reservoirs and weirs, opened irrigation channels, and reclaimed more than two thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wen Qi of Guanghan terraced ponds and canals and opened two thousand qing of new farmland.

sentences.zh: 率厉兵馬，修障塞，降集群夷，甚得其和。

translations.literal: He led and drilled troops and horses, repaired barriers and passes, gathered and pacified the Yi bands, and greatly won their harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled troops, patched the frontier forts, and brought the Yi to peace.

sentences.zh: 及公孫述据益土，齐固守拒險，述拘其妻子，許以封侯，齐遂不降。

translations.literal: When Gongsun Shu held Yizhou, Qi firmly defended and barred the narrows; Shu detained his wife and children and promised him enfeoffment as marquis—Qi then still did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Shu seized his family and offered a marquisate, but Wen Qi held the passes for Han.

sentences.zh: 聞光武即位，乃間道遣使自聞。

translations.literal: Hearing that Guangwu had ascended the throne, he then by hidden routes dispatched envoys to report himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xiu took the throne, Wen Qi sent secret messengers to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，征為镇遠將軍，封成義侯。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was summoned as General Who Guards the Distance and enfeoffed as Marquis Who Completes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell he became General Who Guards the Distance and Marquis of Cheng Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 于道卒，詔為起祠堂，郡人立庙祀之。

translations.literal: He died on the road; an edict ordered a shrine raised for him, and commandery people erected a temple to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: He died en route; the court authorized a shrine and locals built a temple in his honor.

sentences.zh: 建武十八年，夷渠帅栋蚕与姑復、楪榆、梇栋、連然、滇池、建伶、昆明諸种反叛，殺长吏。

translations.literal: Jianwu eighteenth year, Yi channel chief Dongcan together with Gufu, Yeyu, Longdong, Lianran, Dianchi, Jianling, Kunming bands rebelled and killed senior officials.
translations.idiomatic: 42 C.E.: Dongcan’s coalition across western Yunnan murdered Han magistrates.

sentences.zh: 益州太守繁胜与戰而败，退保硃提。

translations.literal: Yizhou Governor Fan Sheng fought them and was defeated; he withdrew to defend Zhuti.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Fan Sheng lost and fell back to Zhuti.

sentences.zh: 十九年，遣武威將軍劉尚等发廣漢、犍為、蜀郡人及硃提夷，合萬三千人擊之。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year, dispatched General Weiwu Liu Shang and others to mobilize Guanghan, Qianwei, and Shu commandery people plus Zhuti Yi, totaling thirteen thousand to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: 43 C.E.: Liu Shang led thirteen thousand from three commanderies and Zhuti tribes.

sentences.zh: 尚軍遂度泸水，入益州界。

translations.literal: Shang’s army then crossed the Lu River and entered Yizhou’s territory.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Lu into Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 群夷聞大兵至，皆弃垒奔走，尚获其赢弱、谷、畜。

translations.literal: The Yi bands hearing great troops arrived all abandoned their ramparts and fled; Shang captured their weak, grain, and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes fled their forts; Han seized grain, stock, and stragglers.

sentences.zh: 二十年，進兵与栋蚕等連戰數月，皆破之。

translations.literal: Twentieth year, advancing troops fought Dongcan and others linked battles several months; all were broken.
translations.idiomatic: 44 C.E.: Months of fighting crushed each band.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，追至不韦，斬栋蚕帅，凡首虏七千余人，得生口五千七百人，馬三千匹，牛羊三萬余頭，諸夷悉平。

translations.literal: The next first month, pursuing to Buwei, they beheaded Dongcan’s chief; in all heads and captives exceeded seven thousand; obtained living captives five thousand seven hundred; horses three thousand; oxen and sheep more than thirty thousand head; the Yi bands were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: At Buwei they slew Dongcan, took seven thousand heads and booty, and ended the rising.

sentences.zh: 肃宗元和中，蜀郡王追為太守，政化尤异。

translations.literal: In Emperor Suzong’s Yuanhe era, Shu commandery’s Wang Zhui became governor; his administration and transformation were especially remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-reign Emperor Zhang: Governor Wang Zhui of Shu was an exemplary ruler.

sentences.zh: 有神馬四匹出滇池河中，甘露降，白烏见，始興起学校，漸迁其俗。

translations.literal: Four divine horses emerged in the Dian Pool river; sweet dew fell; white crows appeared; he first raised schools and gradually shifted their customs.
translations.idiomatic: Portents blessed his schools and quietly reformed frontier manners.

sentences.zh: 靈帝熹平五年，諸夷反叛，执太守雍陟。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling’s fifth Xiping year, the Yi bands rebelled and seized Governor Yong Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: 176 C.E.: Tribes captured Governor Yong Zhi.

sentences.zh: 遣御史中丞硃龟討之，不能克。

translations.literal: He dispatched Imperial Secretary Assistant Zhu Gui to campaign against them; he could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gui’s expedition failed.

sentences.zh: 朝議以為郡在边外，蠻夷喜叛，劳師遠役，不如弃之。

translations.literal: Court debate held the commandery lay beyond the border; Man-Yi delight in rebellion; to weary the army on distant service—better to abandon it.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers argued the distant prefecture was not worth another army.

sentences.zh: 太尉椽巴郡李颙建策討伐，乃拜颙益州太守，与刺史庞芝发板楯蠻擊破平之。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant clerk Li Yong of Ba commandery proposed strategy to campaign; thereupon Li Yong was appointed Yizhou governor; together with Inspector Pang Zhi he mobilized shield-board Man and struck, broke, and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong urged a counterstroke; as governor he and Inspector Pang Zhi used shield-board auxiliaries to win.

sentences.zh: 还，得雍陟。

translations.literal: Returning, they recovered Yong Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: They freed Yong Zhi on the march home.

sentences.zh: 颙卒后，夷人復叛，以廣漢景毅為太守，討定之。

translations.literal: After Yong died, the Yi rebelled again; Guanghan’s Jing Yi was made governor and campaigned to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Yong’s death Jing Yi of Guanghan suppressed the next rising.

sentences.zh: 毅初到郡，米斛萬钱，漸以仁恩，少年間，米至數十云。

translations.literal: When Jing Yi first arrived at the commandery, rice per hu was ten thousand cash; gradually through kindness and grace, within a few years rice reached several tens so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Grain had cost ten thousand cash per hu until his humane rule dropped it to a few dozen.

sentences.zh: 哀牢夷者，其先有妇人名沙壹，居于牢山。

translations.literal: As for the Ailao Yi: their ancestress was a woman named Shayi, who dwelt on Mount Lao.
translations.idiomatic: The Ailao trace a mother named Shayi of Mount Lao.

sentences.zh: 尝捕鱼水中，触沉木若有感，因怀妊，十月，产子男十人。

translations.literal: Once fishing in the water, she touched sunken driftwood as if stirred by feeling; therefore she conceived; in the tenth month she bore ten sons.
translations.idiomatic: Fishing, she touched a submerged log and conceived ten sons.

sentences.zh: 反沉木化為龍，出水上。

translations.literal: Then the sunken driftwood transformed into a dragon and emerged upon the water.
translations.idiomatic: The log became a dragon that broke the surface.

sentences.zh: 沙壹忽聞龍語曰：“若為我生子，今悉何在？

translations.literal: Shayi suddenly heard the dragon speak: ‘You bore sons for me—where are they all now?’
translations.idiomatic: The dragon demanded, ‘Where are the sons you bore for me?’

sentences.zh: ”九子见龍惊走，獨小子不能去，背龍而坐，龍因舐之。

translations.literal: Nine sons saw the dragon and fled in alarm; only the youngest boy could not leave; he sat with his back to the dragon; the dragon therefore licked him.
translations.idiomatic: Nine sons fled; the youngest sat still and let the dragon lick his back.

sentences.zh: 其母鸟語，謂背為九，謂坐為隆，因名子曰九隆。

translations.literal: Their mother spoke bird language: she called ‘back’ jiu and ‘sit’ long; therefore she named the son Jiulong.
translations.idiomatic: In their tongue ‘back’ sounded like jiu and ‘sit’ like long—hence the boy’s name Jiulong.

sentences.zh: 及后长大，諸兄以力隆能為父所舐而黠，遂共推以為王。

translations.literal: When later he grew, his elder brothers, because Jiulong had been licked by the father-dragon and was clever, together acclaimed him as king.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers took the dragon’s blessing as a mandate and enthroned Jiulong.

sentences.zh: 后牢山下有一夫一妇，復生十女子，九隆兄弟皆聚以為妻，后漸相滋长。

translations.literal: Later below Mount Lao there was one husband and one wife who again bore ten daughters; Jiulong’s brothers all gathered them as wives; afterward gradually they multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Ten maidens born below the mountain married Jiulong’s brothers, and the tribe grew.

sentences.zh: 种人皆刻画其身，象龍文，衣皆着尾。

translations.literal: The tribal people all carved and painted their bodies, imaging dragon patterns; their garments all bore tails.
translations.idiomatic: They tattooed dragon patterns and wore skirts like tails.

sentences.zh: 九隆死，世世相继。

translations.literal: When Jiulong died, generation after generation succeeded one another.
translations.idiomatic: Jiulong’s line ruled in turn.

sentences.zh: 乃分置小王，往往邑居，散在溪谷。

translations.literal: Then they divided and placed petty kings; often they dwelt in settlements scattered through ravines and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Petty kings ruled scattered valley towns.

sentences.zh: 絕域荒外，山川阻深，生人以来，未尝交通中國。

translations.literal: Beyond the farthest marches, mountains and rivers perilously deep, since human life began they had never communicated with the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond remote ranges they had never dealt with China.

sentences.zh: 建武二十三年，其王贤栗遣兵乘箄船，南下江、漢，擊附塞夷鹿茤，鹿茤人弱，為所擒获。

translations.literal: Jianwu twenty-third year, their king Xianli dispatched troops riding bamboo rafts south along the Yang and Han to strike the deer-du frontier Yi; the Ludu people were weak and were captured.
translations.idiomatic: 47 C.E.: King Xianli rafted down the Yang and Han and seized the weak Ludu tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 于是震雷疾雨，南風飘起，水為逆流，翻涌二百余里，箄船沉没，哀牢之众，溺死數千人。

translations.literal: Thereupon thunder crashed and rain drove; a south wind rose wildly; the water flowed backward and churned more than two hundred li; the bamboo rafts sank; of the Ailao host several thousand drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Storms reversed the current two hundred li and sank the rafts; thousands of Ailao warriors drowned.

sentences.zh: 贤栗復遣其六王將萬人以攻鹿茤，鹿茤王与戰，殺其六王。

translations.literal: Xianli again dispatched his six kings leading ten thousand men to attack Ludu; the Ludu king fought them and killed his six kings.
translations.idiomatic: Xianli sent six kings with ten thousand men; the Ludu ruler slew all six.

sentences.zh: 哀牢耆老共埋六王，夜虎復出其尸而食之，余众惊怖引去。

translations.literal: Ailao elders together buried the six kings; at night tigers again dug out their corpses and ate them; the remaining host was terrified and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Elders buried the kings until tigers exhumed the bodies; the army fled in horror.

sentences.zh: 贤栗惶恐，謂其耆老曰：“我曹入边塞，自古有之，今攻鹿茤，輒被天诛，中國其有圣帝乎？

translations.literal: Xianli was frightened and said to his elders: ‘We have entered the border fortresses since antiquity; now attacking Ludu we immediately suffer Heaven’s punishment—does the Middle Kingdom have a sage emperor?’
translations.idiomatic: Xianli asked whether Heaven was defending a sage emperor in China.

sentences.zh: 天祐助之，何其明也！

translations.literal: Heaven aids and protects them—how manifest it is!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s favor blazes plain.’

sentences.zh: ”二十七年，贤栗等遂率种人户二千七百七十，口萬七千六百五十九，诣越巂太守郑鸿降，求内屬，光武封贤栗等為君长。

translations.literal: Twenty-seventh year, Xianli and others then led tribal households two thousand seven hundred seventy, persons seventeen thousand six hundred fifty-nine, went to Yuexi Governor Zheng Hong to surrender, requesting internal attachment; Guangwu enfeoffed Xianli and others as chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: 51 C.E.: Xianli brought seventeen thousand followers to Zheng Hong of Yuexi and asked to submit; Guangwu recognized him as chief.

sentences.zh: 自是岁来朝贡。

translations.literal: From this they yearly came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Annual tribute followed.

sentences.zh: 永平十二年，哀牢王柳貌遣子率种人内屬，其种邑王者七十七人，户五萬一千八百九十，口五十五萬三千七百一十一。

translations.literal: Yongping twelfth year, Ailao King Liumao dispatched his son leading tribal people to attach internally; their tribal town kings were seventy-seven persons; households fifty-one thousand eight hundred ninety; persons five hundred fifty-three thousand seven hundred eleven.
translations.idiomatic: 69 C.E.: Liumao’s son led over half a million people and seventy-seven petty kings to submit.

sentences.zh: 西南去洛阳七千里，显宗以其地置哀牢、博南二縣，割益州郡西部都尉所领六縣，合為永昌郡。

translations.literal: Seven thousand li southwest of Luoyang; Emperor Xianzong took their territory and established Ailao and Bonan two counties; carved six counties led by Yizhou commandery’s western commandant and combined them as Yongchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi organized Yongchang commandery from western Yizhou counties plus new Ailao and Bonan seats.

sentences.zh: 始通博南山，度兰仓水。

translations.literal: They first opened through Mount Bonan and crossed the Lancang water.
translations.idiomatic: Han engineers cut the Bonan range and bridged the Lancang.

sentences.zh: 行者苦之。

translations.literal: Travelers suffered for it.
translations.idiomatic: The route broke countless laborers.

sentences.zh: 歌曰：“漢德廣，开不宾。

translations.literal: A song said: ‘Han’s virtue is vast—it draws in those who would not submit.’
translations.idiomatic: Laborers sang of Han’s virtue winning over the unsubmissive.

sentences.zh: 度博南，越兰津。

translations.literal: Cross Bonan; cross Lan Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Cross Bonan; ford the Lan crossing.

sentences.zh: 度兰仓，為它人。

translations.literal: Cross Lancang—we do it for others.
translations.idiomatic: Cross the Lancang—we toil for strangers.

translations.literal: Closing line of the quoted song.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ends the builders’ complaint.

sentences.zh: 哀牢人皆穿鼻儋耳，其渠帅自謂王者，耳皆下肩三寸，庶人則至肩而已。

translations.literal: Ailao people all pierce their noses and distend their ears; their channel chiefs who call themselves kings have ears hanging three inches below the shoulder; commoners’ ears reach only to the shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: Pierced noses and stretched lobes marked status—kings’ ears dangled three inches past the shoulder, commoners’ to the shoulder only.

sentences.zh: 土地沃美，宜五谷、蚕桑。

translations.literal: The land is fertile and fine; it suits the five grains and silkworm mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: Rich soil supported grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 知染采文绣，罽毲帛叠，兰干细布，織成文章如绫锦。

translations.literal: They know dyeing and patterned embroidery, wool piled felts and layered silks, Lan-style fine cloth—woven patterns like damasks.
translations.idiomatic: They dyed embroidery, stacked wool felts, and wove Lan linen rivaling brocade.

sentences.zh: 有梧桐木华，績以為布，幅廣五尺，洁白不受垢污。

translations.literal: There are parasol-tree blossoms spun into cloth five chi wide, pure white and untainted by grime.
translations.idiomatic: Parasol floss wove into five-chi snow-white cloth that stayed clean.

sentences.zh: 先以覆亡人，然后服之。

translations.literal: First they use it to cover the dead; afterward they wear it.
translations.idiomatic: They shrouded the dead in new cloth before wearing it themselves.

sentences.zh: 其竹节相去一丈，名曰濮竹。

translations.literal: Its bamboo joints stand one zhang apart; it is called Pu bamboo.
translations.idiomatic: Pu bamboo had joints a full zhang apart.

sentences.zh: 出铜、铁、铅、锡、金、銀、光珠、虎魄、水精、琉璃、轲虫、蚌珠、孔雀、翡翠、犀、象、猩猩、貊兽。

translations.literal: It yields copper, iron, lead, tin, gold, silver, luminous pearls, amber, rock crystal, colored glass, ‘ke’ shells, mussel pearls, peacocks, kingfisher feathers, rhinoceros, elephant, orangutan, and mo beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Mines and forests yielded metals, gems, glass, shell, feathers, ivory, and exotic pelts.

sentences.zh: 云南縣有神鹿两頭，能食毒草。

translations.literal: Yunnan county has two divine deer that can eat poisonous grass.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan county kept sacred deer that grazed on toxic herbs.

sentences.zh: 先是，西部都尉廣漢郑纯，為政清洁，化行夷貊，君长感慕，皆献土珍，颂德美。

translations.literal: Earlier, Western Commandant Zheng Chun of Guanghan governed cleanly; transformation reached Yi and Mo; chiefs were moved and admired—all presented local treasures and praised his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Commandant Zheng Chun’s honest rule moved tribes to send tribute and sing his praise.

sentences.zh: 天子嘉之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven approved him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 即以為永昌太守。

translations.literal: Immediately made him Yongchang governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted governor of Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 纯与哀牢夷人约，邑豪岁輸布贯頭衣二领，鹽一斛，以為常赋，夷俗安之。

translations.literal: Chun covenanted with Ailao Yi: town magnates yearly delivered two bolt-neck garments of cloth and one hu of salt as regular tax; Yi custom found this acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed a light levy—two tunics and one hu of salt yearly—and the tribes accepted it.

sentences.zh: 纯自為都尉、太守，十年卒官。

translations.literal: Chun himself served as commandant and governor; after ten years he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served ten years as commandant-governor and died in post.

sentences.zh: 建初元年，哀牢王类牢与守令忿争，遂殺守令而反叛，攻巂唐城。

translations.literal: Jianchu first year, Ailao King Leilao quarreled with the guardian magistrate; then killed the guardian magistrate and rebelled; attacked Gutang city.
translations.idiomatic: 76 C.E.: King Leilao slew his magistrate and stormed Gutang.

sentences.zh: 太守王尋奔楪榆。

translations.literal: Governor Wang Xun fled to Yeyu.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Xun fled to Yeyu.

sentences.zh: 哀牢三千余人攻博南，燔烧民舍。

translations.literal: More than three thousand Ailao attacked Bonan and burned commoners’ houses.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand warriors burned Bonan’s outskirts.

sentences.zh: 肃宗募发越巂、益州、永昌夷漢九千人討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong recruited and mobilized nine thousand Yi and Han from Yuexi, Yizhou, and Yongchang to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang drafted nine thousand frontier troops against them.

sentences.zh: 明年春，邪龍縣昆明夷卤承等应募，率种人与諸郡兵擊类牢于博南，大破斬之。

translations.literal: Next spring, Yielong county Kunming Yi Lu Cheng and others answered the levy, led tribal people with various commandery troops to strike Leilao at Bonan, greatly defeated and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Next spring Lu Cheng’s Kunming tribes joined Han columns at Bonan and executed Leilao.

sentences.zh: 传首洛阳，賜卤承帛萬匹，封為破虏傍邑侯。

translations.literal: His head was sent to Luoyang; Lu Cheng was gifted ten thousand bolts of silk and enfeoffed as Marquis Who Breaks Captives at Adjacent Town.
translations.idiomatic: Leilao’s head reached Luoyang; Lu Cheng gained silk and a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 永元六年，郡徼外敦忍乙王莫延慕，遣使譯献犀牛、大象。

translations.literal: Yongyuan sixth year, beyond the commandery march Dunrenyi King Moyanmu dispatched envoys through interpreters to present rhinoceros and elephants.
translations.idiomatic: 94 C.E.: Moyanmu of Dunrenyi sent rhinos and elephants through interpreters.

sentences.zh: 九年，徼外蠻及掸國王雍由调遣重譯奉國珍寶，和帝賜金印紫绶，小君长皆加印绶、钱帛。

translations.literal: Ninth year, march Man and Dian kingdom king Yong Youdiao sent doubled interpreters presenting national treasures; Emperor He bestowed gold seal and purple ribbon; petty chiefs all received seals, ribbons, cash, and silk.
translations.idiomatic: 97 C.E.: Dian’s Yong Youdiao offered tribute through chained interpreters; Emperor He granted gold seals to kings and chiefs.

sentences.zh: 邛都夷者，武帝所开，以為邛都縣。

translations.literal: As for the Qiongdu Yi: Emperor Wu opened them and made Qiongdu county.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu annexed the Qiongdu tribes as a county.

sentences.zh: 無几而地陷為污澤，因名為邛池，南人以為邛河。

translations.literal: Before long the land sank into a foul marsh; therefore it was named Qiong Pool; southerners consider it the Qiong River.
translations.idiomatic: The ground soon sank into Qiong Lake—locals call it the Qiong River.

sentences.zh: 后復反叛。

translations.literal: Later they rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: They rose again.

sentences.zh: 元鼎六年，漢兵自越巂水伐之，以為越巂郡。

translations.literal: Sixth Yuanding year, Han troops from Yuexi water campaigned against them and made Yuexi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: 111 B.C.: Han forces ascended the Yuexi River and organized Yuexi commandery.

sentences.zh: 其土地平原，有稻田。

translations.literal: Its lands are plains; there are paddy fields.
translations.idiomatic: Flat land supported rice paddies.

sentences.zh: 青蛉縣禺同山有碧鸡金馬，光景時時出见。

translations.literal: Qingling county’s Yutong Mountain has azure-rooster and gold horse—lights and glows from time to time appear.
translations.idiomatic: Yutong Mountain near Qingling flashed the legendary Azure Cock and Gold Horse.

sentences.zh: 俗多游荡而喜讴歌，略与牂柯相类。

translations.literal: Custom has much roaming and delights in singing—roughly similar to Zangke.
translations.idiomatic: Their wandering songs recalled Zangke’s frontier ways.

sentences.zh: 豪帅放纵，难得制御。

translations.literal: Magnate chiefs act recklessly; hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: Strongmen defied easy control.

sentences.zh: 王莽時，郡守枚根调邛人长貴，以為軍候。

translations.literal: In Wang Mang’s time, commandery governor Mei Gen summoned Qiong man Changgui and made him a military marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Mei Gen enrolled Changgui as a colonel under Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 更始二年，长貴率种人攻殺枚根，自立為邛穀王。

translations.literal: Gengshi second year, Changgui led tribal people to attack and kill Mei Gen; established himself as King of Qiong Valley.
translations.idiomatic: 24 C.E.: Changgui killed Mei Gen and styled himself king of Qiong Valley.

sentences.zh: 领太守事。

translations.literal: He directed governor affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He assumed civil authority.

sentences.zh: 又降于公孫述。

translations.literal: Again he surrendered to Gongsun Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted to Gongsun Shu.

sentences.zh: 述败，光武封长貴為邛穀王。

translations.literal: When Shu fell, Guangwu enfeoffed Changgui as King of Qiong Valley.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu’s fall Guangwu confirmed Changgui as king.

sentences.zh: 建武十四年，长貴遣使上三年計，天子即授越巂太守印绶。

translations.literal: Jianwu fourteenth year, Changgui dispatched envoys to present the three-year accounting; the Son of Heaven immediately invested him with Yuexi governor’s seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: 38 C.E.: His census mission earned him the Yuexi governor’s seal.

sentences.zh: 十九年，武威將軍劉尚擊益州夷，路由越巂。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year, General Weiwu Liu Shang struck Yizhou Yi; the route passed through Yuexi.
translations.idiomatic: 43 C.E.: Liu Shang’s Yizhou campaign marched through Yuexi.

sentences.zh: 长貴聞之，疑尚既定南边，威法必行，己不得自放纵，即聚兵起营台，招呼諸君长，多酿毒酒，欲先以劳軍，因袭擊尚。

translations.literal: Changgui hearing this, suspected that once Shang had settled the south, awe-inspiring law would surely be enforced and he could no longer indulge himself; immediately gathered troops, raised camp towers, summoned various chiefs, brewed much poisoned wine, wishing first to toast the army and then strike Shang by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Liu Shang would curb him, Changgui staged a poisoned banquet ambush.

sentences.zh: 尚知其谋，即分兵先据邛都，遂掩长貴诛之，徙其家屬于成都。

translations.literal: Shang knew his plot; immediately divided troops to seize Qiongdu first; then surprised Changgui and executed him; relocated his family members to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shang seized Qiongdu first, executed Changgui, and sent his kin to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 永平元年，姑復夷復叛，益州刺史发兵討破之，斬其渠帅，传首京師。

translations.literal: Yongping first year, Gufu Yi rebelled again; Yizhou Inspector mobilized troops to campaign and break them; beheaded their channel chief; sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: 58 C.E.: Gufu tribes rose until the inspector slew their chief and sent his head to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 后太守巴郡張翕，政化清平，得夷人和。

translations.literal: Later Governor Zhang Xi of Ba commandery—administration and transformation clear and fair—won Yi harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Xi of Ba ruled fairly and won the tribes.

sentences.zh: 在郡十七年，卒，夷人爱慕，如丧父母。

translations.literal: Seventeen years in the commandery; when he died, the Yi loved and admired him as if mourning parents.
translations.idiomatic: After seventeen years the tribes mourned him like kin.

sentences.zh: 苏祈叟二百余人，赍牛、羊送丧，至翕本縣安漢，起坟祭祀。

translations.literal: More than two hundred Suqi elders brought oxen and sheep for the funeral procession; reaching Xi’s home county Anhan, they raised a tomb and sacrificed.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred elders drove cattle to Anhan for his burial rites.

sentences.zh: 詔書嘉美，為立祠堂。

translations.literal: An edict praised him beautifully and ordered a shrine erected.
translations.idiomatic: An edict authorized his shrine.

sentences.zh: 安帝元初三年，郡徼外夷大羊等八种，户三萬一千，口十六萬七千六百二十，慕義内屬。

translations.literal: Emperor An’s third Yuanchu year, beyond the commandery march Yi Dayang and eight bands—households thirty-one thousand, persons one hundred sixty-seven thousand six hundred twenty—admired righteousness and attached internally.
translations.idiomatic: 116 C.E.: Eight tribes beyond the march—over 167,000 people—petitioned to submit.

sentences.zh: 時郡縣赋敛烦數，五年，卷夷大牛种封離等反畔，殺遂久令。

translations.literal: At that time commandery and county levies were vexingly frequent; fifth year, Juan Yi Big-Ox band Feng Li and others rebelled and killed Suojiu magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy taxes sparked revolt: Feng Li’s Big-Ox clan killed the Suojiu magistrate in 118 C.E.

sentences.zh: 明年，永昌、益州及蜀郡夷皆叛应之，众遂十余萬，破坏二十余縣，殺长吏，燔烧邑郭，剽略百姓，骸骨委积，千里無人。

translations.literal: The next year, Yongchang, Yizhou, and Shu commandery Yi all rebelled in response; the host then exceeded one hundred thousand; broke more than twenty counties; killed senior officials; burned towns and suburbs; plundered common people; bones piled in heaps; for a thousand li no people.
translations.idiomatic: Next year a hundred-thousand-strong coalition ravaged twenty counties and left borderlands empty.

sentences.zh: 詔益州刺史張乔选堪能从事討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yizhou Inspector Zhang Qiao to select capable assistants to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The court told Inspector Zhang Qiao to appoint able staff to suppress the rising.

sentences.zh: 乔乃遣从事杨竦將兵至□榆擊之，贼盛未敢進，先以詔書告示三郡，密征求武士，重其購赏。

translations.literal: Qiao then dispatched clerk Yang Song to lead troops to [missing graph] Yu to strike them; the bandits were strong and he dared not advance; first he used an edict to proclaim to three commanderies, secretly sought brave warriors, and increased the bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Zhang Qiao sent Yang Song toward Yeyu but held back until edicts mobilized three commanderies and raised bounties for fighters.

sentences.zh: 乃進軍与封離等戰，大破之，斬首三萬余級，获生口千五百人，資财四千余萬，悉以赏軍士。

translations.literal: Then he advanced the army and fought Feng Li and others, greatly defeated them, beheaded more than thirty thousand, captured fifteen hundred living persons, goods and wealth more than forty million—all given to reward soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed Feng Li’s host—thirty thousand heads, fifteen hundred captives, forty million in loot—all paid out to the troops.

sentences.zh: 封離等惶怖，斬其同谋渠帅，诣竦乞降，竦厚加慰纳。

translations.literal: Feng Li and others were terrified; they beheaded their fellow-plotting channel chiefs, went to Song to beg surrender; Song generously consoled and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels executed their own ringleaders and surrendered to Yang Song, who treated them generously.

sentences.zh: 其余三十六种皆来降附。

translations.literal: The remaining thirty-six tribes all came to surrender and attach.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-six other tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 竦因奏长吏奸猾、侵犯蠻夷者九十人，皆减死。

translations.literal: Song therefore memorialized ninety senior officials who were treacherous and encroached on Man-Yi—all had death sentences reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Song impeached ninety abusive Han officials and won commutations.

sentences.zh: 州中论功未及上，会竦病创卒，張乔深痛惜之，乃刻石勒铭，图画其像。

translations.literal: In the province merit discussion had not yet gone up when Song died of battle wounds; Zhang Qiao deeply grieved him; then carved stone and inscribed a eulogy, painted his likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Before his memorial reached court Yang Song died of wounds; Zhang Qiao carved his epitaph and commissioned his portrait.

sentences.zh: 天子以張翕有遗爱，乃拜其子湍為太守。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven because Zhang Xi had surviving love [among the people], then appointed his son Tuan as governor.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring Zhang Xi’s legacy, the emperor named his son Tuan governor.

sentences.zh: 夷人欢喜，奉迎道路。

translations.literal: The Yi rejoiced, welcomed him along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes lined the roads to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 曰：“郎君儀貌类我府君。

translations.literal: They said: ‘The young lord’s bearing resembles our governor.’
translations.idiomatic: They cried that the son looked just like their old prefect.

sentences.zh: ”后湍颇失其心，有欲叛者，諸夷耆老相晓語曰：“当為先府君故。

translations.literal: Later Tuan somewhat lost their hearts; there were some who wished to rebel—Yi elders instructed one another: ‘We should act for the sake of the former governor.’
translations.idiomatic: When Tuan alienated them, elders restrained hotheads out of loyalty to his father.

sentences.zh: ”遂以得安。

translations.literal: Thereby they obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: Peace held.

sentences.zh: 后顺、桓間，廣漢冯颢為太守，政化尤多异迹云。

translations.literal: Later between Shun and Huan, Guanghan’s Feng Hao became governor—administration and transformation had especially many marvels, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperors Shun and Huan, Feng Hao of Guanghan reportedly worked wonders as governor.

sentences.zh: 莋都夷者，武帝所开，以為莋都縣。

translations.literal: As for the Zuodu Yi: Emperor Wu opened them and made Zuodu county.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu organized the Zuodu tribes as a county.

sentences.zh: 其人皆被发左衽，言語多好譬类，居處略与汶山夷同。

translations.literal: Their people all wear loose hair and left-lapped robes; speech mostly delights in metaphor and analogy; dwellings roughly resemble Wenshan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: They wore hair loose and robes left-lapped, spoke in vivid analogies, and lived like the Wenshan tribes.

sentences.zh: 土出长年神药，仙人山图所居焉。

translations.literal: The soil yields longevity elixirs; immortal Mountain Diagram dwells there.
translations.idiomatic: The hills yielded longevity herbs and legend placed immortals there.

sentences.zh: 元鼎六年，以為沈黎郡。

translations.literal: Sixth Yuanding year, it was made Shenli commandery.
translations.idiomatic: 111 B.C.: Han organized Shenli commandery.

sentences.zh: 至夭漢四年，并蜀為西部，置两都尉：一居旄牛，主徼外夷；

translations.literal: By fourth Tianhan year [text reads 夭漢], merged with Shu as the western division, established two commandants: one dwelling at Maoniu, supervising march-exterior Yi;
translations.idiomatic: 97 B.C.: The west was split between two command posts—Maoniu handled frontier tribes;

sentences.zh: 一居青衣，主漢人。

translations.literal: one dwelling at Qingyi, supervising Han people.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyi supervised Han settlers.

sentences.zh: 永平中，益州刺史梁國硃輔，好立功名，慷慨有大略。

translations.literal: In Yongping times, Yizhou Inspector Zhu Fu of Liang state loved establishing merit and fame; impassioned and grand in strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping-era Inspector Zhu Fu was ambitious and strategically bold.

sentences.zh: 在州數岁，宣示漢德，威怀遠夷。

translations.literal: Several years in the province, he proclaimed Han virtue and awed and cherished distant Yi.
translations.idiomatic: For years he showcased Han virtue and won distant tribes.

sentences.zh: 自汶山以西，前世所不至，正朔所未加。

translations.literal: West from Wenshan—what former ages never reached, where correct calendar was never applied.
translations.idiomatic: West of Wenshan lay lands Han calendars had never reached.

sentences.zh: 白狼、槃木、唐菆等百余國，户百三十余萬，口六百萬以上，舉种奉贡，种為臣僕。

translations.literal: Bailang, Panmu, Tangcou and more than one hundred states—households more than 1.3 million, persons more than six million—whole tribes presented tribute; tribes became servants.
translations.idiomatic: Over a hundred polities—more than six million people—sent tribute and accepted subject status.

sentences.zh: 輔上疏曰：“臣聞《詩》云：‘彼徂者岐，有夷之行。

translations.literal: Fu submitted a memorial saying: ‘Your servant has heard the Classic of Poetry says: “Those who went to Qi had the Way of the Yi.”’
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fu quoted the ‘Qi’ ode on civilization reaching barbarians.

sentences.zh: ’传曰：‘岐道雖僻，而人不遠。

translations.literal: The commentary says: “Though Qi road is remote, people are not distant.”’
translations.idiomatic: Commentators say even remote Qi drew people in.’

sentences.zh: ’詩人诵咏，以為符验。

translations.literal: Poets chant it as verification.’
translations.idiomatic: Poets took it as proof.’

sentences.zh: 今白狼王唐菆等慕化歸義，作詩三章。

translations.literal: Now Bailang king Tangcou and others admire transformation and return to righteousness; they composed three poems.
translations.idiomatic: King Tangcou of the Bailang composed three hymns of submission.’

sentences.zh: 路经邛来大山零高坂，峭危峻險，百倍岐道。

translations.literal: The road passes Qionglai’s great mountain Linggao slope—sheer, perilous, and deadly—a hundredfold worse than Qi road.
translations.idiomatic: Their route over Qionglai’s cliffs dwarfed the old Qi road in danger.’

sentences.zh: 襁負老幼，若歸慈母。

translations.literal: Carrying old and young on their backs—as if returning to a loving mother.
translations.idiomatic: They bore children to court like pilgrims to a mother.’

sentences.zh: 遠夷之語，辞意难正。

translations.literal: Far Yi speech—its wording and meaning are hard to rectify.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier languages resist literal glosses.’

sentences.zh: 草木异种，鸟兽殊类。

translations.literal: Plants and trees are alien kinds; birds and beasts peculiar sorts.
translations.idiomatic: Their flora and fauna differ utterly from China.’

sentences.zh: 有犍為郡掾田恭与之习狎，颇晓其言，臣輒令訊其風俗，譯其辞語。

translations.literal: There is Qianwei commandery clerk Tian Gong intimate with them who fairly understands their speech; your servant then ordered him questioned on their customs and to translate their wording.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Tian Gong knew their tongue; I had him translate custom and idiom.’

sentences.zh: 今遣从事史李陵与恭护送诣阙，并上其乐詩。

translations.literal: Now dispatching clerk-scribe Li Ling with Gong to escort them to the palace and submit together their music-poems.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ling and Tian Gong escort the envoys and deliver the songs.’

sentences.zh: 昔在圣帝，舞四夷之乐；

translations.literal: Anciently under sage emperors they danced the music of the four Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sage-kings staged barbarian dances;

sentences.zh: 今之所上，庶备其一。

translations.literal: what is submitted now perhaps supplies one part.
translations.idiomatic: these hymns may add one strain.’

sentences.zh: ”帝嘉之，事下史官，錄其歌焉。

translations.literal: The emperor praised them; the matter went down to historians who recorded their songs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and ordered the songs archived.

sentences.zh: 《遠夷乐德歌詩》曰：

translations.literal: The ‘Song of Distant Yi Delighting in Virtue’ says:
translations.idiomatic: Song of the Distant Yi on Delighting in Virtue (title)

sentences.zh: 大漢是治，堤官隗构。

translations.literal: Great Han is order [Yi]: Diguan Weigou.
translations.idiomatic: Great Han rules in peace; the emperor matches Heaven’s pattern.

sentences.zh: 与天合意。

translations.literal: Join with Heaven’s intent.
translations.idiomatic: His mind accords with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 魏冒逾糟。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Weimao Yuzao.
translations.idiomatic: His grace overflows like rivers crossing brine.

sentences.zh: 吏譯平端，罔驿劉脾。

translations.literal: Officials and interpreters fair and upright [Yi]: Wangyi Liupi.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates and interpreters deal fairly—none cheat the frontier.

sentences.zh: 不从我来。

translations.literal: Those who would not follow me.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever refuses to follow us—

sentences.zh: 旁莫支留。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Pangmozhiliu.
translations.idiomatic: —finds nowhere to hide.

sentences.zh: 聞風向化，征衣隨旅。

translations.literal: Hearing the wind turn to transformation; travel clothes following the embassy.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing your virtue we turned to civilization and packed our cloaks for the journey.

sentences.zh: 所见奇异。

translations.literal: What we saw was strange and marvelous.
translations.idiomatic: What we saw amazed us.

sentences.zh: 知唐桑艾。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Zhitangsang’ai.
translations.idiomatic: We knew King Tangcou’s kindness.

sentences.zh: 多賜缯布，邪毘纟甚纟甫。

translations.literal: Much granted silk cloth [Yi]: Xiepishenfu (corrupt graphs).
translations.idiomatic: You piled silk and fine cloth on us.

sentences.zh: 甘美酒食。

translations.literal: Sweet fine wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet wine and rich food.

sentences.zh: 推潭僕遠。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Tuitan Puyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Our gratitude runs deep from afar.

sentences.zh: 昌乐肉飞，拓拒苏便。

translations.literal: Bright joy—meat flies [Yi]: Tuoju Subian.
translations.idiomatic: Festive platters and piping music rose together.

sentences.zh: 屈申悉备。

translations.literal: Bent and stretched—all fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Every flavor—sour and sweet—was spread.

sentences.zh: 局后仍離。

translations.literal: After the feast still we depart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after the banquet we must leave.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷贫薄，偻让龍洞。

translations.literal: Man-Yi poor and thin [Yi]: Lou rang longdong.
translations.idiomatic: We poor barbarians in bamboo huts—

sentences.zh: 無所報嗣。

translations.literal: Nothing wherewith to repay and continue.
translations.idiomatic: —have no way to repay you.

sentences.zh: 莫支度由。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Mozhiduyou.
translations.idiomatic: We bring no worthy gift in return.

sentences.zh: 愿主长寿，阳雒僧鳞。

translations.literal: Wish the lord long life [Yi]: Yangluo Senglin.
translations.idiomatic: We pray our lord lives many years—

sentences.zh: 子孫昌炽。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons blaze bright.
translations.idiomatic: —and sons and grandsons flourish forever.

sentences.zh: 莫稚角存。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Mozhijiaocun.
translations.idiomatic: May none of your house lack grain.

sentences.zh: 《遠夷慕德歌詩》曰：

translations.literal: The ‘Song of Distant Yi Admiring Virtue’ says:
translations.idiomatic: Song of the Distant Yi on Admiring Virtue (title)

sentences.zh: 蠻夷所處，偻让皮尼。

translations.literal: Where Man-Yi dwell [Yi]: Lou rang pini.
translations.idiomatic: We barbarians live where the sun sets—

sentences.zh: 日入之部。

translations.literal: The regions where the sun enters.
translations.idiomatic: —in the sunset lands.

sentences.zh: 且交陵悟。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Qiejiaolingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains pile ridge upon ridge.

sentences.zh: 慕義向化，绳动隨旅。

translations.literal: Admiring righteousness, turning to transformation; cords stir—follow the embassy.
translations.idiomatic: Yearning for Han righteousness we harnessed horses and joined your envoys.

sentences.zh: 歸日出主。

translations.literal: Return—sunrise lord.
translations.idiomatic: We turned toward the rising-sun sovereign.

sentences.zh: 路旦拣雒。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Ludan jianluo.
translations.idiomatic: Long roads wound toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 圣德深恩，圣德渡诺。

translations.literal: Sage virtue—deep grace; sage virtue—crossing consent.
translations.idiomatic: Sage virtue grants boundless grace—boundless as a ford.

sentences.zh: 与人富厚。

translations.literal: Giving people wealth and thickness.
translations.idiomatic: You enrich every household.

sentences.zh: 魏菌度洗。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Weijun Duxi.
translations.idiomatic: Your mercy washes us clean.

sentences.zh: 冬多霜雪，综邪流籓。

translations.literal: Winter much frost and snow [Yi]: Zongxie Liufan.
translations.idiomatic: Winters heap frost and snow on our ranges.

sentences.zh: 夏多和雨。

translations.literal: Summer much harmonious rain.
translations.idiomatic: Summers bring gentle rains.

sentences.zh: 莋邪尋螺。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Zuoxie Xunluo.
translations.idiomatic: Cold and heat arrive in season.

sentences.zh: 寒温時适，藐浔沪漓。

translations.literal: Cold and warmth timely fitting [Yi]: Miaoxun Huli.
translations.idiomatic: Seasons suit sowing and harvest.

sentences.zh: 部人多有。

translations.literal: The tribe’s people greatly abound.
translations.idiomatic: Our people multiply.

sentences.zh: 菌补邪推。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Junbu Xietui.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings crowd every valley.

sentences.zh: 涉危历險，辟危歸險。

translations.literal: Cross peril, traverse danger; avoid peril, return to danger.
translations.idiomatic: We braved cliffs and rapids—yet pressed on toward grace.

sentences.zh: 不遠萬里。

translations.literal: Not deeming ten thousand li distant.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand li did not deter us.

sentences.zh: 莫受萬柳。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Moshou Wanliu.
translations.idiomatic: No hardship turned us back.

sentences.zh: 去俗歸德，术叠附德。

translations.literal: Leave custom, return to virtue [Yi]: Shudie Fude.
translations.idiomatic: We shed barbarous ways and clung to Han virtue.

sentences.zh: 心歸慈母。

translations.literal: Hearts return to loving mother.
translations.idiomatic: Our hearts flew to a loving mother.

sentences.zh: 仍路孳摸。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Renglü Zimo.
translations.idiomatic: We traced the road ever homeward to Han.

sentences.zh: 《遠夷怀德歌》曰：

translations.literal: The ‘Song of Distant Yi Cherishing Virtue’ says:
translations.idiomatic: Song of the Distant Yi on Cherishing Virtue (title)

sentences.zh: 荒服之外，荒服之儀。

translations.literal: Beyond wild tribute zones—wild tribute zones’ demeanor.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the wild outer march—yet we observe ceremony.

sentences.zh: 土地墝埆。

translations.literal: Land stony and thin.
translations.idiomatic: Our soil is barren rock.

sentences.zh: 犁籍怜怜。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Liji Lianlian.
translations.idiomatic: Fields cling to steep slopes.

sentences.zh: 食肉衣皮，阻苏邪犁。

translations.literal: Eat meat, wear hides [Yi]: Zusu Xieli.
translations.idiomatic: We ate flesh and wore hides against the cold.

sentences.zh: 不见鹽谷。

translations.literal: Do not see salt valleys.
translations.idiomatic: We knew neither salt pans nor grain valleys.

sentences.zh: 莫砀粗沐。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Modang Cumu.
translations.idiomatic: We rarely tasted grain or bath.

sentences.zh: 吏譯传風，罔譯传微。

translations.literal: Officials and interpreters transmit customs [Yi]: Wangyi Chuanwei.
translations.idiomatic: Your clerks and interpreters carried word of civilization.

sentences.zh: 大漢安乐。

translations.literal: Great Han peaceful joy.
translations.idiomatic: Great Han is peace and joy.

sentences.zh: 是漢夜拒。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Shi Han Yeju.
translations.idiomatic: This is the Han that welcomes night wanderers.

sentences.zh: 携負歸仁，踪优路仁。

translations.literal: Carrying burdens—return to benevolence [Yi]: Zongyou Luren.
translations.idiomatic: We bore packs toward benevolence—every road led to grace.

sentences.zh: 触冒險陕。

translations.literal: Brush perilous defiles.
translations.idiomatic: We climbed deadly passes.

sentences.zh: 雷折險龍。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Leizhe Xianlong.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder split the ridge-dragons.

sentences.zh: 高山岐峻，伦狼藏幢。

translations.literal: High mountains fork steep [Yi]: Lunlang Zangchuang.
translations.idiomatic: Peaks forked like wolves guarding banners.

sentences.zh: 缘崖磻石。

translations.literal: Along cliffs tread stone.
translations.idiomatic: We edged cliffs on stepping stones.

sentences.zh: 扶路側禄。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Fulu Celu.
translations.idiomatic: We hugged the trails along the slope.

sentences.zh: 木薄发家，息落服淫。

translations.literal: Thin trees rise from houses [Yi]: Xiluo Fuyin.
translations.idiomatic: Brush broke through hovels—we laid hardship aside.

sentences.zh: 百宿到洛。

translations.literal: Hundred lodgings reach Luo.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred halts brought us to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 理历髭雒。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Lili Ziluo.
translations.idiomatic: At last we looked upon the Luo’s shores.

sentences.zh: 父子同賜，捕顡菌毘。

translations.literal: Father and son together granted [Yi]: Bu’ai Junpi.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers and sons shared your gifts together.

sentences.zh: 怀抱匹帛。

translations.literal: Embrace bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: We clasp bolts of silk to our breasts.

sentences.zh: 怀稿匹漏。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Huaigao Pilou.
translations.idiomatic: We tuck drafts of tribute beneath our arms.

sentences.zh: 传告种人，传室呼敕。

translations.literal: Transmit and tell the tribal kind; transmit chamber—call the command.
translations.idiomatic: Word passes tribe to tribe—every hearth hears the summons.

sentences.zh: 长愿臣僕。

translations.literal: Forever willing to be servants.
translations.idiomatic: Forever we choose servitude to Han.

sentences.zh: 陵阳臣僕。

translations.literal: [Yi]: Lingyang chenpu.
translations.idiomatic: May we remain loyal servants under the sun.

sentences.zh: 肃宗初，輔坐事免。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Suzong’s reign, Fu was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhang’s reign Zhu Fu lost his post over a charge.

sentences.zh: 是時郡尉府舍皆有雕飾，画山神海靈、奇禽异兽，以眩耀之，夷人益畏惮焉。

translations.literal: At that time commandant headquarters all had carved ornamentation, painted mountain gods and sea spirits, strange birds and beasts—to dazzle them; the Yi grew more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural command posts boasted murals of spirits and beasts that awed the tribes.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元十二年，旄牛徼外白狼、楼薄蠻夷王唐缯等，遂率种人十七萬口，歸義内屬。

translations.literal: Emperor He’s Yongyuan twelfth year, beyond Maoniu march Bailang, Loubo Man-Yi king Tang Zeng and others then led tribal kind one hundred seventy thousand persons to attach in righteousness internally.
translations.idiomatic: 100 C.E.: Tang Zeng led 170,000 Bailang and Loubo tribesmen beyond Maoniu to submit.

sentences.zh: 詔賜金印紫绶，小豪钱帛各有差。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed gold seal and purple ribbon; petty magnates cash and silk each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted gold seals and graded gifts of silk to lesser chiefs.

sentences.zh: 安帝永初元年，蜀郡三襄种夷与徼外污衍种并兵三千余人反叛，攻蚕陵城，殺长吏。

translations.literal: Emperor An’s Yongchu first year, Shu commandery Three-Xiang band Yi with march-exterior Wuyan band joined troops more than three thousand rebelled, attacked Canling city, killed senior officials.
translations.idiomatic: 107 C.E.: Three-Xiang and Wuyan tribes took Canling and slew Han officers.

sentences.zh: 二年，青衣道夷邑长令田，与徼外三种夷三十一萬口， 赍黄金、 旄牛毦，舉土内屬。

translations.literal: Second year, Qingyi-road Yi town chief Ling Tian with three march-exterior Yi bands three hundred ten thousand persons, bearing gold and yak-tail wool, offered their territory to attach internally.
translations.idiomatic: 108 C.E.: Chief Ling Tian brought 310,000 tribesmen and tribute of gold and yak felt to submit.

sentences.zh: 安帝增令田爵号為奉通邑君。

translations.literal: Emperor An advanced Ling Tian’s noble title to Lord of Fengtong Town.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An ennobled him as Lord of Fengtong.

sentences.zh: 延光二年春，旄牛夷叛，攻零关，殺长吏，益州刺史張乔与西部都尉擊破之。

translations.literal: Yanguang second year spring, Maoniu Yi rebelled, attacked Ling Pass, killed senior officials; Yizhou Inspector Zhang Qiao with Western Commandant struck and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: 123 C.E.: Maoniu tribes stormed Ling Pass until Zhang Qiao and the western commandant crushed them.

sentences.zh: 于是分置蜀郡屬國都尉，领四縣如太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon separately established Shu commandery dependent-state commandant, overseeing four counties like a governor.
translations.idiomatic: Han created a dependent-state commandant over four counties with governor-like powers.

sentences.zh: 桓帝永寿二年，蜀郡夷叛，殺略吏民。

translations.literal: Emperor Huan’s Yongshou second year, Shu commandery Yi rebelled, killed and plundered officials and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: 156 C.E.: Shu tribes raided officials and settlers.

sentences.zh: 延熹二年，蜀郡三襄夷寇蚕陵，殺长吏。

translations.literal: Yanxi second year, Shu commandery Three-Xiang Yi raided Canling, killed senior officials.
translations.idiomatic: 159 C.E.: Three-Xiang tribes struck Canling again.

sentences.zh: 四年，犍為屬國夷寇郡界，益州刺史山昱擊破之，斬首千四百級，余皆解散。

translations.literal: Fourth year, Qianwei dependent-state Yi raided commandery borders; Yizhou Inspector Shan Yu struck and broke them; beheaded fourteen hundred grades; remainder all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: 161 C.E.: Shan Yu killed 1,400 raiders and dispersed the rest.

sentences.zh: 靈帝時，以蜀郡屬國為漢嘉郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling’s time, took Shu commandery dependent state as Hanjia commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ling the dependent state became Hanjia commandery.

sentences.zh: 冉駹夷者，武帝所开，元鼎六年，以為汶山郡。

translations.literal: As for the Ranmao Yi: Emperor Wu opened them; sixth Yuanding year, made Wenshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu organized the Ranmao lands as Wenshan commandery in 111 B.C.

sentences.zh: 至地节三年，夷人以立郡赋重，宣帝乃省并蜀郡為北部都尉。

translations.literal: By third Dijie year, the Yi because establishing the commandery levies were heavy, Emperor Xuan then abolished and merged into Shu commandery as northern commandant.
translations.idiomatic: 67 B.C.: Heavy taxes prompted Emperor Xuan to fold Wenshan into Shu as a northern commandant.

sentences.zh: 其山有六夷七羌九氐，各有部落。

translations.literal: Its mountains have six Yi, seven Qiang, nine Di—each with tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Six Yi, seven Qiang, and nine Di bands held the range.

sentences.zh: 其王侯颇知文書，而法严重。

translations.literal: Their kings and marquises fairly understand documents, yet law is stern and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs could read documents but enforced harsh law.

sentences.zh: 貴妇人，党母族。

translations.literal: They esteem women; they factionalize maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: They honored women and maternal clans.

sentences.zh: 死則烧其尸。

translations.literal: When dead then burn their corpses.
translations.idiomatic: They cremated the dead.

sentences.zh: 土气多寒，在盛夏冰犹不释，故夷人冬則避寒，入蜀為佣，夏則違暑，反其邑。

translations.literal: Soil and vapor much cold—even in midsummer ice still does not melt; therefore Yi in winter then avoid cold, enter Shu as hired labor; in summer then flee heat, return to their settlements.
translations.idiomatic: Perpetual snow sent them to Shu as winter laborers and home for summer.

sentences.zh: 众皆依山居止，累石為室，高者至十余丈，為邛笼。

translations.literal: All dwell leaning on mountains; pile stone for chambers—the high reach more than ten zhang; called qionglong towers.
translations.idiomatic: They stacked stone towers—qionglong—ten zhang high on the slopes.

sentences.zh: 又土地刚卤，不生谷粟麻菽，唯以麦為資，而宜畜牧。

translations.literal: Moreover land is hard and briny; does not grow grain, millet, hemp, beans—only take wheat as resource; yet suits herding.
translations.idiomatic: Barren soil grew only barley but fed vast herds.

sentences.zh: 有旄牛，無角，一名童牛，肉重千斤，毛可為毦。

translations.literal: There are yak cattle, hornless; another name ‘boy cattle’; flesh weighs a thousand jin; hair can make wool felt.
translations.idiomatic: Hornless yak weighed a thousand jin—felt from their wool.

sentences.zh: 出名馬。

translations.literal: Yields famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: The range bred famed horses.

sentences.zh: 有靈羊，可疗毒。

translations.literal: There are spirit sheep that can cure poison.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit sheep yielded antidotes.

sentences.zh: 又有食药鹿，鹿鏖有胎者。

translations.literal: Moreover there are drug-eating deer—pregnant hinds.
translations.idiomatic: Drug-grazing hinds carried valued pregnancies.

sentences.zh: 其肠中粪亦疗毒疾。

translations.literal: Their intestinal dung also cures poison illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: Even dung from their guts countered venom.

sentences.zh: 又有五角羊、麝香、轻毛<曷毛>鸡、牲牲。

translations.literal: Moreover five-horned sheep, musk deer, light-feather he-mao chickens, and shēng-shēng [legendary beasts].
translations.idiomatic: Five-horned sheep, musk, silky fowl, and mountain apes entered trade.

sentences.zh: 其人能作旄氈、班罽、青顿、毞毲、羊羧之屬。

translations.literal: Their people can make yak felt, patterned wool, green dun, pitui woolens, sheep-suan kinds.
translations.idiomatic: They wove yak felt, patterned rugs, and piled woolens.

sentences.zh: 特多杂药。

translations.literal: Especially many miscellaneous drugs.
translations.idiomatic: Medicinal herbs abounded.

sentences.zh: 地有咸土，煮以為鹽。

translations.literal: Ground has salty soil; boil to make salt.
translations.idiomatic: Brine earth boiled into salt.

sentences.zh: 麡羊牛馬，食之皆肥。

translations.literal: Qiyi sheep, oxen, horses—eating it all grow fat.
translations.idiomatic: Argali, cattle, and horses fattened on the grass and salt.

sentences.zh: 其西又有三河、槃于虏，北有黄石、北地、卢水胡，其表乃為徼外。

translations.literal: West of them again have Sanhe, Panyulu; north have Huangshi, Beidi, Lushui Hu—beyond their surface then is march-exterior.
translations.idiomatic: West lay Sanhe and Panyulu; north lay Hu bands—the outer zone lay beyond the pale.

sentences.zh: 靈帝時，復分蜀郡北部為汶山郡云。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling’s time, again divided Shu commandery’s north as Wenshan commandery, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling restored Wenshan commandery from northern Shu.

sentences.zh: 白馬氐者，武帝元鼎六年开，分廣漢西部，合以為武都。

translations.literal: As for White Horse Di: sixth Yuanding year Emperor Wu opened them, divided Guanghan west and combined as Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: White Horse Di became Wudu commandery in 111 B.C. from western Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 土地險阻，有麻田，出名馬、牛、羊、漆、蜜。

translations.literal: Land perilous and obstructed; there are hemp fields; yields famous horses, oxen, sheep, lacquer, honey.
translations.idiomatic: Steep land grew hemp and famed herds plus lacquer and honey.

sentences.zh: 氐人勇戆抵冒，贪货死利。

translations.literal: Di people brave and blunt—rush hazards; greedy for goods, die for profit.
translations.idiomatic: The Di were reckless fighters who chased profit without fear.

sentences.zh: 居于河池，一名仇池，方百顷，四面斗絕。

translations.literal: They dwell at Hechi—another name Qiuchi—a hundred qing square; on four sides steeply sheer.
translations.idiomatic: They held Qiu Pool—a hundred-qing basin walled by cliffs.

sentences.zh: 數為边寇，郡縣討之，則依固自守。

translations.literal: Repeatedly became border raiders; when commanderies and counties campaign against them, they rely on fastness and defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They raided the frontier yet holed up in their fortress whenever attacked.

sentences.zh: 元封三年，氐人反叛，遣兵破之，分徙酒泉郡。

translations.literal: Third Yuanfeng year [Emperor Wu], Di people rebelled; dispatched troops broke them; divided and relocated to Jiuquan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: 108 B.C.: Han crushed a Di rising and deported clans to Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 昭帝元凤元年，氐人復叛，遣执金吾馬適建、龍<名页>侯韩增、大鸿胪田廣明，將三輔、太常徒討破之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhao’s first Yuanfeng year, Di rebelled again; dispatched Bearer of the Mace Ma Shijian, Long[e]-marquis Han Zeng, Grand Herald Tian Guangming, leading Sanfu and Taichang convicts to campaign and break them.
translations.idiomatic: 80 B.C.: Ma Shijian, Han Zeng, and Tian Guangming led capital levies against another Di revolt.

sentences.zh: 及王莽篡亂，氐人亦叛。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang usurped and threw things into chaos, Di also rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang’s coup sparked Di risings.

sentences.zh: 建武初，氐人悉附陇蜀，及隗嚣灭，其酋豪乃背公孫述降漢，陇西太守馬援上復其王侯君长，賜以印绶。

translations.literal: Early Jianwu, Di all attached to Long and Shu; when Wei Xiao perished, their chiefs then turned from Gongsun Shu and surrendered to Han; Longxi Governor Ma Yuan memorialized restoring their kings, marquises, and chiefs, bestowing seals and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Xiao fell, Ma Yuan restored Di titles when they abandoned Gongsun Shu for Han.

sentences.zh: 后嚣族人隗茂反，殺武都太守。

translations.literal: Later Wei Xiao’s clansman Wei Mao rebelled, killed Wudu governor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mao later murdered the Wudu governor.

sentences.zh: 氐人大豪齐钟留為种类所敬信，威服諸豪，与郡丞孔奋擊茂，破斬之。

translations.literal: Di great magnate Qi Zhongliu was revered and trusted by the tribes; awed and subdued various magnates; with assistant governor Kong Fen struck Mao, broke and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Magnate Qi Zhongliu rallied the Di behind Kong Fen and executed Wei Mao.

sentences.zh: 后亦時為寇盗，郡縣討破之。

translations.literal: Later also from time to time became raiding bandits; commanderies and counties campaigned and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Later raids were crushed piecemeal.

sentences.zh: 论曰：漢氏征伐戎狄，有事边遠，盖亦与王业而终始矣。

translations.literal: The assessment says: Han’s campaigns against Rong and Di, undertaking affairs in distant borders—generally also began and ended with the royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Han’s frontier wars against Rong and Di shadowed the dynasty from rise to fall.

sentences.zh: 至于倾没疆垂，丧師败將者，不出時岁，卒能开四夷之境，款殊俗之附。

translations.literal: As for drowning in border marches, losing armies and defeated generals—not beyond a few years; ultimately able to open four-Yi territory and sincerely attach exotic customs.
translations.idiomatic: Though borders sank and generals fell almost yearly, Han still opened four quarters and drew distant peoples in.

sentences.zh: 若乃文约之所沾漸，風声之所周流，几將日所出入處也。

translations.literal: As for where civil compact has soaked and steeped, where tone and voice circulate—it nearly reaches wherever sun rises and sets.
translations.idiomatic: Han prestige and rumor reached nearly every place under the sun.

sentences.zh: 著自山经、水志者，亦略及焉。

translations.literal: What is recorded from Mountain Classic and Water Treatises—also touches on them in outline.
translations.idiomatic: Even mountain and water gazetteers sketch these lands.

sentences.zh: 雖服叛难常，威澤時曠，及其化行，則缓耳雕脚之伦，兽居鸟語之类，莫不舉种尽落，回面而請吏，陵海越障，累譯以内屬焉。

translations.literal: Although submission and rebellion are hard to keep constant, awe and bounty sometimes lapse—yet when transformation proceeds, then slack-eared and carved-foot sorts, beast-dwelling bird-speaking kinds—none fail to raise whole tribes and bands, turn faces and request officials, cross seas and pass barriers, chained interpreters to attach internally.
translations.idiomatic: Despite fitful loyalty, when civilization took hold even tattooed tribes turned to ask for magistrates—crossing seas and interpreters to submit.

sentences.zh: 故其錄名中郎、校尉之署，編數都护、部守之曹，动以數百萬計。

translations.literal: Therefore their recording names at Gentleman Attendant and Colonel offices; roster counts at Protector-General and department governor bureaus—movements reckoned in millions.
translations.idiomatic: Hence attendant and colonel registers and protector rolls numbered in the millions.

sentences.zh: 若乃藏山隐海之靈物，沉沙栖陆之玮寶，莫不呈表怪丽，雕被宫幄焉。

translations.literal: As for spirit creatures hiding mountains and seas, rare treasures sunk in sand resting on land—none fail to display strange splendor, carved and draped on palace curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Marvelous beasts and sunken treasures adorned the palace—all tribute from afar.

sentences.zh: 又其賨幏火毳、驯禽封兽之赋，軨积于内府；

translations.literal: Moreover their cong cloth, fire wool, tame fowl and sealed beasts tribute—wheel-loads pile in inner treasury;
translations.idiomatic: Tribute wool, feathers, and captive beasts filled the imperial vaults;

sentences.zh: 夷歌巴舞、殊音异节之技，列倡于外门。

translations.literal: Yi songs and Ba dances; strange tones and exotic rhythms’ arts—array performers at outer gates.
translations.idiomatic: frontier songs and Ba dances lined the outer courts.

sentences.zh: 岂柔服之道，必足于斯？

translations.literal: Could it be that the Way of soft submission must suffice in this?
translations.idiomatic: Was gentle rule nothing more than spectacle?

sentences.zh: 然亦云致遠者矣。

translations.literal: Yet one may say they reached the distant.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Han truly reached the ends of the earth.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷雖附阻岩谷，而类有土居，連涉荆、交之区，布护巴、庸之外，不可量极。

translations.literal: Man-Yi although cling blocking cliffs and valleys, yet mostly have earth dwellings—linked spanning Jing and Jiao regions, spread guarding beyond Ba and Yong—cannot measure the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes clung to ravines yet formed settlements—stretching from Jing and Jiao past Ba and Yong beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 然其凶勇狡算，薄于羌狄，故陵暴之害，不能深也。

translations.literal: Yet their fierce bravery and cunning schemes are thinner than Qiang and Di; therefore bullying harm cannot go deep.
translations.idiomatic: They were less fierce than Qiang or Di—so their raids rarely cut deep.

sentences.zh: 西南之徼，尤為劣焉。

translations.literal: Southwestern marches—especially more inferior therein.
translations.idiomatic: The southwest marches were weaker still.

sentences.zh: 故关守永昌，肇自遠離，启土立人，至今成都焉。

translations.literal: Therefore guarding Yongchang—begun from distant separation—opening soil, establishing people—down to today Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yongchang’s garrison—opened from distant lands—still anchors Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 赞曰：百蠻蠢居，仞彼方徼。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Hundred Man dwell stupidly—blade-high those border marches.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Myriad tribes thronged those distant marches.

sentences.zh: 镂体卉衣，凭深阻峭。

translations.literal: Carve bodies, flower garments—lean on deep perilous crags.
translations.idiomatic: Tattooed skin and grass robes clung to sheer defiles.

sentences.zh: 亦有别夷，屯彼蜀表。

translations.literal: Also there are other Yi—encamped beyond Shu’s edge.
translations.idiomatic: Other tribes camped beyond Shu’s rim.

sentences.zh: 参差聚落，纡余岐道。

translations.literal: Uneven settlements; winding surplus forked roads.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered hamlets threaded winding passes.

sentences.zh: 往化既孚，改襟輸寶。

translations.literal: Going transformation already trusted—change lapels, convey treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Once trust bloomed they turned lapels and sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 俾建永昌，同編亿兆。

translations.literal: Cause to establish Yongchang—together register with hundred-million masses.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang rose to share in the myriad subjects of Han.
